## Architecture

**Rust decides, AVFoundation and Metal do** (spec §7). The core holds the
project (JSON, spec §5.2), every edit, the composition plan, the per-frame
recipe, the index of a WebM/Matroska file being imported and the WebM file an
`av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` or `vp9_alpha_webm` export writes (its container only; the packets come from Swift). Swift owns windows, gestures, undo, AVFoundation playback and export,
the Metal compositor, media import and its caches and on-device analysis of
the media (Vision and Sound Analysis on the analysis lane, cached per media
in `cache/analysis/`; the core reads only what a tool or op hands it), and
agent dispatch. No
pixel or sample work in Rust; no ffmpeg dependency in the product. The AV1 and
VP9 encoders (SVT-AV1, libvpx; `designs/adr/codec-export.md`) are
platform-side like AVFoundation: Swift calls them through the bridging header,
no `rc_*` export wraps them (spec §11 CX-4).

### FFI contract

- `core/include/framejob_core.h` is a **hand-maintained** C header, the single
  contract between the worlds. **The FFI is three files in lockstep**: a Rust
  `#[no_mangle]` export, its entry in the header, and its wrapper in
  `app/Sources/ReelCore.swift` and its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, **the
  only files that call `rc_*`** (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in
  the file of its area.
- A handle is an immutable project. **Every edit is pure and answers one of
  three arms** (`core/src/outcome.rs`, spec §5.5): applied with the new
  project, an identity, or refused in the rule's own sentence. Only the first
  is an undo step. `ProjectDocument` is the single mutation point and undo is
  its stack of handles.
- Edits are JSON ops through `rc_project_apply`. **The op table is two
  halves**: what an op MEANS is the module doc of `core/src/edit.rs`, and
  what it TAKES — every argument's name, kind and required-ness — is
  `core/src/op_table.rs`, as data, published as JSON Schema by
  `rc_op_schemas`. `ReelOps.swift`'s typed builders,
  `AgentCatalog*.swift`'s tools and spec §6 mirror them — change one, change
  all four — **except that every op TOOL prints the arguments half instead of
  restating it** (`AgentCatalog.opTool`), so an argument added to an op costs
  a sentence of prose there and no schema. A tool that takes more or less
  than its op does says so in `AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift`, one row and
  one reason each. The envelope's `scope` key addresses an edit inside a
  nest.
- Persisted-state changes bump `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `core/src/format.rs`
  **and** the header.
- Errors: `rc_project_apply` returns NULL three distinguishable ways, and the
  two message channels are never both written. NULL with NEITHER written is
  an identity; NULL with `reason_out` set is a refusal and that string is the
  rule's own sentence; NULL with `err_out` set is invalid input. The first two
  make no undo step and only the third is an error. `"internal error: …"` is a
  caught panic.

### Where a feature lands — the standard recipe

Every shipped feature follows the same shape; putting a step's code anywhere
else is what bloats files:

1. **Core:** the op's semantics in an `impl Project` block in the module of
   its own concern (a new concern is a new module); the row in `edit.rs`'s
   enum and module-doc table, and its arguments in `op_table.rs` (which is
   where `OP_NAMES` comes from); a persisted field with a serde default and a
   `schema_vN.rs`; a new `core/tests/*.rs`. A field lands in the same phase as
   the thing that renders it.
2. **FFI**, only when a new `rc_*` export is needed: Rust → header →
   the ReelCore file of its area.
3. **Swift:** the typed builder in `ReelOps.swift`; a small value or model
   file; an `EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift` with its validator arm; an
   inspector section REGISTERED in `ClipPane.makeSections()`; a menu item in
   `AppDelegate+Menus.swift`; a gesture as a session struct.
4. **MCP mirror:** a handler in `AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`, a catalog entry
   declaring `scope`, and a comment naming the UI path it mirrors.
5. **Documents:** spec §5.2 / §6 / §7.10 for anything they mirror; the map
   entry in the per-side `CLAUDE.md` if a file's role changed; the feature's
   page in `docs/guide/` (and its README highlight and
   `menus-and-shortcuts.md` row when it adds one); the phase's record in its
   road map.
6. **Verify:** as "Verification" below says; then read the change back
   adversarially before committing.

## Rules

- Conventions are Rasterize's — `~/devel/rasterize`'s three `CLAUDE.md`
  files are the parent text for anything not settled here.
- **Every user-visible edit gets an MCP mirror** (spec §7.9): a handler, a
  catalog entry, and a comment naming the UI path. The startup parity check
  in `AgentServer.prepareCatalog()` has SIX parts: catalog names against handler
  names, every op in the core's table against the tools (through
  `rc_op_names`, with an explicit allow-list for ops that deliberately have
  none), each tool's schema shape, that every op tool declares `scope`,
  that every op tool declares the CORE's own arguments for its op — each one
  described, and no description for an argument no op has
  (`AgentServer+Parity.swift`), and that every tool `ModelKeys.keyed` names
  exists and its description carries its key's clause
  (`AgentServer+Parity.swift`, spec §11 CJ-13). What it cannot see is a CALL, which two
  things guard at dispatch: the argument GATE in `AgentServer+Gate.swift`
  compares the caller's keys to the schema the tool published and refuses a
  stranger by name, for all one hundred and twenty-five product tools (and the dev tools,
  road map 11), before any handler runs;
  and the throwing helpers in `AgentServer+Arguments.swift` refuse a value a
  handler cannot read by name rather than dropping it.
- **A feature that needs a language or cloud model tests its key through
  `ModelKeys`** (spec §11 CJ-3): presence, the sentence, the control's or
  menu item's mark, the tool's refusal where it would send, and a row in
  `ModelKeys.keyed`.
- **A file at the ~600-line cap gives something up before it takes anything
  on**, as a pure move landed and gated alone; new files are capped at 400
  lines. Frozen files take wiring only. `core/src/edit.rs` and
  `app/Sources/ReelOps.swift` are exempt (tables, one row per op), and proof
  instruments in `tools/proof/` are held to neither cap. The ledger is
  `wc -l app/Sources/*.swift core/src/*.rs graphic/src/*.rs | sort -rn`; the
  seam a record already named for a file is under "Named next cuts" in
  `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` / `core-file-history.md`.
- **Size rules are per FILE, never per feature.** A brief, design, road map,
  spec or proof never sets a budget on how many lines a feature may add,
  never measures a feature's total against one, and never names code size as
  a reason to cut, trim or drop a feature: a feature takes as much code as it
  needs. Keeping files small is the cap above and its pure moves, nothing
  else (owner, 2026-10-10).
- **A decision in spec §11 is not re-litigated** (`designs/spec/11-decisions/`). A phase that needs a new
  one records it there before the code, not after.
- **`.secrets/` (gitignored) holds the owner's own keys for proofs**, e.g.
  `.secrets/anthropic-key`, read ONLY by `anthropic_key()` in
  `tools/proof/assistant_prompt_eval.py`. Never open, print, grep, copy or
  list its contents; never move a key from it into an argument, the
  environment of a build, a log or a file. A run that spends money still
  needs its explicit flags (`--live --cap <dollars>`); the file's presence
  spends nothing. Every paid proof request is also held to the month's
  budget (spec §11 P-3, P-6) in
  `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job Proofs/spend.jsonl`; an agent
  never edits it, raises a budget, or points a verification at it.
- **A check only a person at the machine can make is a row in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`**, added in the change that creates it — never a
  `ready-for-human` issue, and never an instrument built to stand in for the
  person (how a pane looks, whether audio plays, a real key's conversation).
  Automate what a script can truly measure; list only the residue.
- Commit only when asked. A commit message says what was verified and what
  is owed, and the road map's record says the same.

## Verifying a build

A local Distribution build is only ever checked, never launched: it loads
Sparkle, which library validation refuses in an ad-hoc signed hardened app
(spec §11 PUB-7). Debug and Release link with `-dead_strip_dylibs`, so they
never load it.

The app is verified by driving the built binary over MCP and comparing what
it renders — not by reading code. Launch your own instance on your own socket
and only ever kill that one (`pgrep -f "MacOS/Frame Job"` lists them, Debug
and Release alike; the products folder tells them apart; another session may
have one running):

```sh
make app-debug
python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch   # prints folder, socket, log, pid
```

Each later command names the printed folder literally
(`mcp.MCP("<dir>/agent.sock")`, `python3 tools/proof/phaseN_proof.py
<dir>/agent.sock`, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`), because a shell
variable does not survive from one agent command to the next; stop it by the
pid the launcher prints.

The log line `Frame Job agent socket listening at <dir>/agent.sock` says it is
up (`not bound: <reason>` says why not). Drive it with `tools/proof/mcp.py`'s
`mcp.MCP("<dir>/agent.sock")` (streamable HTTP over the Unix socket), or with
the bundled stdio helper `framejob-mcp` with `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` set to the same
path: one tool per §6 op, each taking the `scope`
envelope key, plus the app-state tools — `open_project`, `new_project`,
`new_project_from_range`, `save_project`, `close_project`, `get_project`, `import_media`,
`import_captions`, `export_captions`, `transcribe`, `consolidate_media`, `detect_silence`,
`detect_fillers`, `transcribe_for_fillers`, `get_transcript`, `get_timeline_transcript`, `get_media_analysis`, `split_at_shots`, `normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio`, `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection`, `set_scope`,
`undo`, `redo`, `render_frame`, `export`, `export_status`, `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `cancel_export`,
`record_screen`, `write_graphic`,
`get_graphic`, `graphic_reference`, `render_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`,
`import_graphic_asset`, `delete_graphic`, `rename_graphic`,
`restore_graphic`, `list_graphics`, `insert_graphic`, `export_graphic` and `import_graphic`. A Debug or Release build also has the dev tools
(`snapshot_ui`, `perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`;
"Seeing the chrome" below; `play_preview`, which plays a window's preview
for a while and answers the frames composed (#127, spec §11 G-36);
`graphic_memory`, which answers the graphic rasters' memory budget, what is
held and kept, and simulates memory pressure (G-37); `loudness_meter`, which
answers a window's live loudness meter (momentary, short-term, integrated,
true peak, the frames measured and its resets) and resets it (road map
"audio" AP7, AU-77); `land_recording`, which lands fixture files as a
finished recording through the recorder panel's door or `record_screen`'s,
so a proof can watch Enhance the microphone when it lands without a
microphone grant (spec §11 AU-69); and
`analysis_job`, which wants a media's analysis under a document's stand-in
owner and returns at once, or waits for every such job and answers their
runs (spec §11 CJ-27); and `-RCDevAnalysisHold <s>`, which holds each
analysis job before its first frame, polling cancellation, so a proof can
act during it; and `-RCDevAnalysisCanned YES`, with which a canned analysis
marker is honoured (spec §11 CJ-26); and `transcript_view`, which answers

A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. An instance DEADLOCKS somewhere past forty documents open at once:
a proof that closes what it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and
one that does not relaunches between proof sessions.

Spec §10's per-step verifications are the acceptance tests. What no script
can answer — step 4's "the clip plays with audio", step 5's 60 fps, and the
rest — is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which the owner runs.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A failed current or reference build is a scored failure,
including an FFI diagnostic; it is never a historical skip or a reason to
fall back to the old harness. Only the recording proof's granted tier can
skip rows for a named host condition such as a locked console.

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:

=================== actions
---
title: Actions
description: What an action is, how it takes a clip to an end state over a span of time, and how numbers, colours and switches change along the way.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

An action makes a clip change over time: a zoom into a screen recording, a fade of the volume, a title that slides and changes colour. You say where the clip ends up, and the action's span and curve say how it gets there.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', "A band on the clip in the timeline"]}
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
/>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.window"
  alt="The editor with a lower third selected. On the timeline the graphic clip holds a numbered action band, the Clip tab's action lane reads 1, editing 1, and the inspector shows the values the clip reaches at the action's end."
/>

## What an action is

An action is a span of time on one clip. Over that span, the clip's properties move from whatever they were when the span began to the action's **end state**, along the action's curve.

Actions take the place of keyframes. You don't set a value at each moment. You set what the clip ends at, and the span and the curve do the rest.

=================== motion-presets
---
title: Motion presets
description: Give a clip a ready-made entrance, exit or continuous movement that's tied to its two ends and stays with it through a trim.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A motion preset says what a clip does rather than where it is: how it arrives, how it leaves and what it does in between. It's tied to the clip's two ends, so it goes with the clip through a trim and there's nothing to reposition afterwards.

Each clip has three slots, and all three can run on the same clip:

- **In** is an entrance at the clip's start: Fade, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Slide Left, Slide Right, Slide Up, Slide Down, Spin or Pop. See [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/).
- **Out** is an exit at the clip's end, from the same nine kinds.
- **During** is a movement for the clip's whole length: Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce or Drift. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).

Presets work on any clip that draws a picture: video, still images, text, shapes, graphics and nests.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Out', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview']}
  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
  tools="set_video"
/>

## Give a clip a preset

<Steps>

1. Select the clip.

2. In the Clip tab, pick the **Clip** sub-tab and open **Motion presets**, the last section. It's closed by default.

3. Choose a kind from **In**, **Out** or **During**.

4. Set **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or for a During movement, **Amount** and **Period**.

5. Choose **Preview** to watch it loop.

</Steps>

If the defaults suit you, [the Motion menu](#use-the-motion-menu) is quicker.

=================== motion-presets
---
title: Motion presets
description: Give a clip a ready-made entrance, exit or continuous movement that's tied to its two ends and stays with it through a trim.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A motion preset says what a clip does rather than where it is: how it arrives, how it leaves and what it does in between. It's tied to the clip's two ends, so it goes with the clip through a trim and there's nothing to reposition afterwards.

Each clip has three slots, and all three can run on the same clip:

- **In** is an entrance at the clip's start: Fade, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Slide Left, Slide Right, Slide Up, Slide Down, Spin or Pop. See [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/).
- **Out** is an exit at the clip's end, from the same nine kinds.
- **During** is a movement for the clip's whole length: Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce or Drift. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).

Presets work on any clip that draws a picture: video, still images, text, shapes, graphics and nests.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Out', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview']}
  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
  tools="set_video"
/>

## Give a clip a preset

<Steps>

1. Select the clip.

2. In the Clip tab, pick the **Clip** sub-tab and open **Motion presets**, the last section. It's closed by default.

3. Choose a kind from **In**, **Out** or **During**.

4. Set **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or for a During movement, **Amount** and **Period**.

5. Choose **Preview** to watch it loop.

</Steps>

If the defaults suit you, [the Motion menu](#use-the-motion-menu) is quicker.

42	## What an action is
43	
44	An action is a span of time on one clip. Over that span, the clip's properties move from whatever they were when the span began to the action's **end state**, along the action's curve.
45	
46	Actions take the place of keyframes. You don't set a value at each moment. You set what the clip ends at, and the span and the curve do the rest.
47	
48	Actions on one clip can't overlap, and you can't make one that runs past the clip's end. A later trim can leave an action running past the end, and only the part inside the clip plays. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
49	
50	To make one, see [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), then [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
51	
52	## The end state is held
53	
54	When the span is over, the clip keeps the end state until a later action changes it. An action that takes the scale to 200% leaves the clip at 200% for the rest of its length. The clip doesn't drift back on its own.
55	
56	To go back, add a second action whose end state names the old value. [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) does this for a zoom.
57	
58	## Clip time
59	
60	An action's times are measured from the clip's own start, not from the start of the timeline. An action that starts at 2 seconds starts 2 seconds into the clip, wherever the clip sits. Move the clip and its actions go with it.
61	
62	The start field in the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) shows this time.
63	
64	## Several actions on a clip
65	
66	A clip can have as many actions as fit end to end. They run in time order, and each one starts from the state the earlier ones left behind.
67	
68	An action only changes what its end state names. If action 1 takes the scale to 200% and action 2 names only the opacity, the scale stays at 200% through action 2 while the opacity moves.
69	
70	## Action numbers
71	
72	Actions are numbered in time order, and an action has the same number on the timeline and in the Clip tab. The number is a position, not a name, so adding an action before an existing one moves the later ones up by one. If two actions ever share a start, the older one comes first.
73	
74	## Easing curves
75	
76	A curve sets how a value moves across the span. The same four curves serve actions, zooms, speed ramps and transitions.
77	
78	| Curve | In the action lane | How it moves | Halfway through the span, the value is |
79	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
80	| Linear | Linear | At a constant speed | 50% of the way there |
81	| Ease In | In | Starts slowly, ends fast | 25% of the way there |
82	| Ease Out | Out | Starts fast, ends slowly | 75% of the way there |
83	| Ease In Out | In Out | Slow at both ends | 50% of the way there |
84	
85	The action lane's curve pop-up shows the short names, with a small drawing of the curve beside it. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/). A transition's **Curve** pop-up shows the full names. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
86	
87	### Default curves
88	
89	A new action from **Add Action** is **Linear**. A zoom action, from Zoom to Region or Zoom Back, is **Ease In Out**.
90	
91	## How values change over an action
92	
93	What happens to a property depends on what kind of value it is. [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/) goes through them section by section.
94	
95	### Numbers
96	
97	Numbers ramp along the action's curve. That covers position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, volume, a filter's amount, a grade's sliders and a graphic's number properties.
98	
99	An agent can aim a number past what the property can hold. Frame Job keeps the value in the action as written and brings it into range as the clip is drawn, so an opacity aimed at 200% reaches 100% before the action ends and stays there.
100	
101	### Colours
102	
103	Most colours ramp too, through OKLab, which keeps the blend's midpoints even. A cursor's **Ripple color** switches at the end instead. See [Colours blend in OKLab](/motion/what-can-animate/#colours-blend-in-oklab).
104	
105	### Switches, pop-ups and text
106	
107	An on/off box, a filter's kind, a font and a graphic's string, boolean or image property have nothing in between. They hold their value for the whole span, then switch to the end value when the action ends. Once the action changes one, its row in the Clip tab is tagged "at end".
108	
109	The same goes for a section you turn on inside an action, such as a shadow or an outline. Its numbers have nothing to ramp from, so it appears whole when the action ends.
110	
111	:::tip
112	To fade a shadow in, turn it on for the clip with **Opacity** at 0%, then add an action that raises **Opacity**. The opacity ramps, because both ends of it exist.
113	:::
114	
115	### Lists
116	
117	Filters and obscure regions are lists, and they ramp entry by entry while both ends have the same number of entries.
118	
119	| If | Then |
120	| --- | --- |
121	| Both ends have the same number of entries | Each entry's numbers ramp to the entry in the same place at the other end |
122	| One entry changes kind, or a region changes shape | Only that entry switches at the end, and the others still ramp |
123	| The list's length changes | The whole list switches at the end |
124	
125	### Colour curves
126	
127	Curves in the **Color** sub-tab always animate. Two curves with the same number of points ramp point by point, and a neutral curve lines up with the other curve's points. Two curves with different numbers of points blend their values over the action.
128	
129	## With an agent
130	
131	`add_action`, `set_action`, `set_action_end` and `remove_action` do everything the Clip tab does with an action. An agent names the curves `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` and `ease_in_out`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

149	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
150	
151	Add Action puts a new [action](/motion/actions/) on the selected clip at the playhead, ready for you to say what it animates to.
152	
153	<AtAGlance
154	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"

160	## Add Action
161	
162	<Steps>
163	
164	1. Select a clip and put the playhead over it.
165	
166	2. Press <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Add Action** and the **+** button in the Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) do the same.
167	
168	3. In the Clip tab, change what you want the clip to reach by the end of the action. To fade the clip out over that second, for example, set **Opacity** in the **Picture** sub-tab to 0%.
169	
170	</Steps>
171	
172	The new action starts at the playhead, lasts 1 second and uses the **Linear** curve. It's one undo step.
173	
174	## A new action starts empty
175	
176	A new action's end state is empty, so it changes nothing until you edit it. The band appears, and the clip looks and sounds the same as before.
177	
178	The action is selected as it's added, so the Clip tab is ready for its end state. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/). The playhead stays where it is, at the action's start, so the preview shows the change only once you move through the action or play it.
179	
180	## When Add Action is available
181	
182	Add Action needs the playhead over a selected clip. Otherwise **Clip ▸ Add Action** is greyed out, and the action lane's **+** button beeps.
183	
184	## Several clips selected
185	
186	With several clips selected, the action goes on the first selected clip under the playhead and isn't selected, because only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Select that clip alone to edit the new action.
187	
188	## When there's no room for an action
189	
190	The new action needs a clear second after the playhead. Frame Job beeps and adds nothing when the action would:
191	
192	- overlap another action on the clip, or
193	- run past the clip's end.
194	
195	The reason appears at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:". See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
196	
197	Near the end of a clip, move the playhead back first, or [shorten an existing action](/motion/change-an-action/). A clip shorter than 1 second has no room for an action from Add Action.
198	
199	## Other commands that make actions
200	
201	These commands write ordinary actions. They show as bands and edit like any other.
202	
203	| Command | What it adds |
204	| --- | --- |
205	| [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) | One 1-second **Ease In Out** action that zooms to a rectangle you draw |
206	| [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/#zoom-back) | One 1-second **Ease In Out** action back to the clip's own size and place |
207	| [Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) | One action for Ramp Up and Ramp Down, two for Speed Dip and Speed Burst |
208	| [Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…](/recording/auto-zoom/) | Zoom actions planned from a recording's cursor file |
209	| [Clip ▸ Follow Subject…](/framing/follow-subject/) | Moves that keep a subject in frame |
210	| [Clip ▸ Camera Layout](/framing/camera-layouts/) | Moves from one layout to the next |
211	| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | An action for each point you add with <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click |
212	
213	Only Add Action, Zoom to Region and Zoom Back select the action they make.
214	
215	## With an agent
216	
217	`add_action` takes the clip, a start in clip time and an optional length, 1 second if left out, so an agent can place an action shorter than 1 second where Add Action has no room. The new action's id comes back in `new_actions`. See [`add_action`](/mcp/tools-animation/#add_action).

247	## Click a band
248	
249	Click an action's band on the timeline or in the Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). The action is selected, and the Clip tab then edits its end values.
250	
251	The playhead moves to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing. When the action ends with the clip, the playhead stops one frame short, because the clip's very end has no picture.
252	
253	Clicking a band on a clip that's part of a multi-clip selection selects only that clip and its action.
254	
255	On the timeline the action is selected when you press. In the Clip tab's lane it's selected when you let go, so a drag in the lane selects the band when you drop it. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
256	
257	## Adding selects the action
258	
259	An action made with [Add Action](/motion/add-an-action/), [Zoom to Region or Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/) is selected as it's added. The playhead doesn't move for this.
260	
261	## Play or scrub into a span
262	
263	While a clip is the only one selected, moving the playhead into one of its actions selects that action. Playing, scrubbing and stepping all count.
264	
265	Selecting a clip counts too. If the playhead is already inside one of its actions, that action is selected along with the clip.
266	
267	The playhead has to enter the span. An edit that puts a span under a still playhead selects nothing, and neither does an undo or a redo.
268	
269	## How a selected action looks
270	
271	On the timeline:
272	
273	- The action's band is solid.
274	- A wash runs down the clip under the action's span.
275	- The span is shaded on the ruler.
276	
277	In the Clip tab:
278	
279	- The action lane is tinted, and its header adds "· editing N" after the count.
280	- The band is solid, and the **Clip** chip is no longer highlighted.
281	- A detail row appears with the action's start, length, curve and trash button.
282	
283	## The Clip chip
284	
285	The **Clip** chip sits at the start of the action lane. It's highlighted while no action is selected, which tells you the fields edit the clip. Click it while an action is selected to leave the action.
286	
287	## Leave an action
288	
289	Do any of these, and the Clip tab shows the clip's own values again:
290	
291	- Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>.
292	- Click the **Clip** chip.
293	- Select a different clip.
294	
295	Moving the playhead out of the span doesn't leave the action. It stays selected, and the fields keep editing its end state.
296	
297	After <kbd>Esc</kbd> or the **Clip** chip, the playhead can stay inside the span without selecting the action again. It's selected the next time the playhead leaves and comes back.
298	
299	With no action selected, <kbd>Esc</kbd> does whatever it would do otherwise.
300	
301	## Selection is not an edit
302	
303	Selecting an action isn't an undo step, and it isn't saved with the project. A project always opens with no action selected.
304	
305	## Good to know
306	
307	- Only a single selected clip can have a selected action. Select a second clip and the action is deselected. The action lane then reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."
308	- Where two bands sit under the pointer, the one painted on top wins, which is the later one.
309	- Clicking a band that touches the next action puts the playhead on the first frame of that next action, but the one you clicked stays selected.
310	- Removing the selected action deselects it.
311

341	## Bands on the timeline
342	
343	A clip that has an action shows a lane directly under its name strip, with one band per action. Each band spans the action's time on the clip, and is at least 2 pt wide however short the action is.
344	
345	Actions are numbered in time order, so a band's number is its place on the clip, and moving an action past another changes both numbers. The number is the same on the timeline and in the Clip tab.
346	
347	Click a band to select the clip and that action. The playhead moves to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing. Drag a band's body to move the action, or a grip to resize it. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/) and [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
348	
349	The selected action's band is solid. A wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler.
350	
351	A band on a locked track doesn't respond. It doesn't highlight, and clicking it selects the clip, not the action.
352	
353	### Band detail by track height
354	
355	How much a band shows depends on [**View ▸ Timeline Track Height**](/timeline/track-height/).
356	
357	| Track height | Lane height | A band shows |
358	| --- | --- | --- |
359	| Small | 5 pt | A plain bar. |
360	| Medium | 12 pt | Its number, a zoom glyph for a zoom action, and the curve on the selected band. |
361	| Large | 18 pt | All of that, plus the properties it changes, such as `scale, x, y` or `speed`. A graphic's animated properties are listed with the clip's other properties. |
362	
363	The zoom glyph is a small magnifier. It appears on any action that changes exactly scale, x and y, however the action was made.
364	
365	From Medium, a clip whose rate moves also draws its rate line over the bands. While the line is there, a selected Speed band doesn't draw its curve. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).
366	
367	### Band hover
368	
369	Point at a band, on the timeline or in the Clip tab's lane, and it brightens and shows a 5 pt grip at each end. The pointer is an open hand over the body and a resize arrow over a grip.
370	
371	A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips, so you can only move it. On the timeline, zoom in to make it wider.
372	
373	## The action lane in the Clip tab
374	
375	The action lane is a small timeline of the selected clip. It's pinned at the top of the Clip tab, between the clip's name and the sub-tabs, so it stays put while you scroll the sections below. The whole clip always fits the lane's width, however long it is.
376	
377	### Header row
378	
379	The header reads **ACTIONS**, then the number of actions or "none". While action N is selected, it adds "· editing N". The three buttons at its right end are:
380	
381	| Button | Tooltip | What it does |
382	| --- | --- | --- |
383	| Zoom-in magnifier | Zoom to Region (Z) | Lets you draw a rectangle on the canvas to zoom to. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/). |
384	| Zoom-out magnifier | Zoom Back | Adds an action that returns the clip to its own scale and position. See [Zoom Back](/motion/zoom-to-region/#zoom-back). |
385	| Plus | Add Action (⌥⌘K) | Adds an action at the playhead. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). |
386	
387	While you drag a band in the lane, a readout takes the place of the header's text, with times counted from the clip's start. The buttons stay.
388	
389	### Lane row
390	
391	The **Clip** chip sits at the left. It's highlighted while no action is selected, and clicking it deselects the action, so the Clip tab goes back to editing the clip itself.
392	
393	To its right is the whole clip, with its actions as numbered bands and the playhead as a thin line. Click or drag a band here as you would on the timeline. These bands show their number, the zoom glyph and the selected band's curve whatever the track height, and never list properties. A clip whose rate moves draws its rate line here too.
394	
395	A clip with no actions shows "no actions · ⌥⌘K adds one".
396	
397	### What else the lane shows
398	
399	Under the bands, the lane draws the same marks the timeline draws for the clip, so you can place an action around them:
400	
401	| Mark | Where | Shown when |
402	| --- | --- | --- |
403	| Hatching | At the clip's start, as long as the overlap | The clip has a [transition](/motion/transitions/) and overlaps the clip before it. |
404	| Fades | Triangles along the bottom, at either end | The clip has sound and a fade in or out. |
405	| Motion wedges | Triangles hanging from the top, at either end | The clip has an active In or Out [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/). |
406	
407	### Detail row
408	
409	This row appears only while an action is selected. Its fields have no labels, so read them from left to right as they're listed here. Each change is one undo step.
410	
411	| Control | What it does | Range |
412	| --- | --- | --- |
413	| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode measured from the clip's own start. | |
414	| Length | How long the action takes, in seconds, snapped to whole frames. | 0.01 to 36,000 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2. A longer value is held to the clip's length. |
415	| Curve | How the action eases from its start to its end state, with a glyph of the curve beside it. | Linear, In, Out, In Out |
416	| Trash button | Removes the action. <kbd>⌫</kbd> does the same. | |
417	
418	If Frame Job can't take a typed Start or Length, for example because the action would overlap another or run past the clip's end, it beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:". The line stays until the project next changes or you click it.
419	
420	### Several clips selected
421	
422	With several clips selected the lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions.", and there's no count, Clip chip, bands or detail row.
423	
424	The three buttons stay. Add Action still works, and puts the action on the first selected clip under the playhead without selecting it. Zoom to Region and Zoom Back need a single clip, so they beep.
425	
426	## The gutter mark
427	
428	While an action is selected, each row of the Clip tab it animates has a ◆ in its left gutter. Hover over the ◆ and it turns into ×, with the tooltip "Remove from action N". Click it to take that row out of the action, as one undo step, Remove from Action. The row's right-click menu has the same command.
429	
430	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for all the marks and what they mean.

466	## Edit the end state
467	
468	<Steps>
469	
470	1. [Select the action](/motion/select-an-action/). Clicking its band also moves the playhead to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing.
471	
472	2. Change any row in the Clip tab. Type a value, drag a slider, pick from a pop-up or choose a colour.
473	
474	3. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the clip travel to what you set.
475	
476	</Steps>
477	
478	While an action is selected, every field shows the value the clip reaches at the action's end, and every edit writes that value. Changing a row adds it to the action, and the row gets a ◆.
479	
480	Your edits follow the selected action, not the playhead. If the playhead wanders out of the action's span, the action stays selected and the fields keep showing its end. If it moves into another action's span on the clip, that action becomes the selected one.
481	
482	To edit the clip itself again, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or click the [**Clip** chip](/motion/select-an-action/#the-clip-chip) at the start of the action lane.
483	
484	What happens along the way depends on the kind of value. Numbers and most colours ramp along the action's curve, and switches, pop-ups and text hold and then change at the end. See [How values change over an action](/motion/actions/#how-values-change-over-an-action).
485	
486	## Edit on the canvas
487	
488	With an action selected, the canvas writes the end state too. Moving, scaling, rotating or cropping the clip, dragging a text clip's wrap width and dragging an obscure region all change that action's end, not the clip.
489	
490	The box on screen still shows the frame at the playhead, while a drag starts from the end state and changes it by the distance you drag. With the playhead partway through the action, the box moves only part of the way. Work with the playhead at the action's end, which is where clicking the band puts it, and the box lands where you let go.
491	
492	Two things on the canvas always edit the clip itself:
493	
494	- A drag on a multi-clip selection. Only a single selected clip can have a selected action.
495	- Resizing a shape's box, or dragging a line's or arrow's end points. A shape's own properties can't animate. Moving a shape still writes the action's end.
496	
497	## Switch a property off
498	
499	Untick a switch inside an action and that property turns off when the action ends. **Drop shadow**, a text clip's **Outline** and **Backdrop**, and sound switches such as **Limit peaks** all work this way, and so does a single band of the EQ.
500	
501	The property stays on through the action, then goes off as it ends. The row shows ◆ and "at end".
502	
503	This is different from [taking the row out of the action](#take-a-property-out-of-the-action), which stops the action changing the property at all.
504	
505	## Read the row marks
506	
507	Each row in the Clip tab has a narrow gutter to the left of its label. The mark there says how the row relates to the selected action.
508	
509	| Mark | What it means | How else you can tell |
510	| --- | --- | --- |
511	| ◆ | This action animates the row. | The label turns strong, and a field or pop-up gets a border in the action colour. |
512	| ◇ | Another action on the clip animates the row. | Its tooltip reads "Changed by action N". |
513	| ○ | The row follows a value this action animates. **Gain** follows **Volume**, for example. | |
514	| ⊘ | Actions don't animate this row, so an edit here changes the clip. | The label turns faint. |
515	
516	With an action selected, a blank gutter usually means the row can animate and nothing is animating it yet. It isn't a promise: a few controls carry no mark and still change the clip, such as **In**, **Out** and **Reverse** in the Timing section.
517	
518	◇ also shows when no action is selected, on every row an action on the clip animates. It's a quick way to see what's moving before you pick an action.
519	
520	The **Normalize** button changes the clip whatever is selected. While an action is selected a small boxed **clip** tag follows it, and the tag's tooltip reads "Actions don't animate this. It changes the clip."
521	
522	### The "at end" tag
523	
524	A control that can't blend says "at end" beside it once the action animates it. It holds its old value until the action ends, then switches.
525	
526	Pop-ups, checkboxes, segmented controls and text fields all work this way. Most colours ramp, but a few can't blend, such as a cursor's ripple colour, and those say "at end" too.
527	
528	## See the value change as it plays
529	
530	With an action selected, the field reads the value at the action's end. The rest of the row shows how it gets there.
531	
532	**On a slider**, the rail fills in the action colour from the value at the action's start to the knob. A coral tick marks the value at the playhead. The tick shows whenever the playhead is inside the clip and that value differs from the knob, even with no action selected.
533	
534	**On a row with no slider**, a coral tag gives that value in words, such as "now 1.50×". It shows while the playhead is inside the clip and the value there differs from the field.
535	
536	## Read the sections and sub-tabs
537	
538	Section headers carry the same marks as their rows:
539	
540	- **◆N** counts what the selected action animates in that section.
541	- **◇** means another action animates a row in the section.
542	- **⊘** means every row in the section is ⊘, and the section also says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip."
543	
544	The summary at the right of a header turns the action colour when the action animates the section.
545	
546	### Sub-tab counts
547	
548	Each sub-tab's label shows **◆N** when the selected action animates N things on it, so you can see what an action does without opening every tab.
549	
550	| Sub-tab | What counts |
551	| --- | --- |
552	| Picture | Each property. A zoom action reads ◆3, for its scale and its two position values. |
553	| Color | Light and Color together count as one. Look, Wheels, Curves and Qualifier count as one each, however many values inside them change. On an adjustment clip, Strength counts as one too. |
554	| Sound | Each property. |
555	| Text | Each property. |
556	| Graphic | Each property the action animates. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/). |
557	| Clip | A speed change, as ◆1. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/). |
558	| Shape | Nothing, ever. A shape's own properties can't animate. |
559	
560	### Sections open by themselves
561	
562	Selecting an action opens the sections it animates on the sub-tab you're looking at, and they stay open for as long as that action is selected. A sub-tab you switch to later opens its own animated sections the first time it shows.
563	
564	Close one by hand and it stays closed while that action is selected. Opening by itself doesn't change your own layout: leave the action and the sections it opened go back to how you had them.
565	
566	## Take a property out of the action
567	
568	Taking a property out stops the action changing it. The row falls back to what the clip held before the action, and the action itself stays.
569	
570	| To take out | Do this | Undo step |
571	| --- | --- | --- |
572	| One row | Hover over its ◆ and click the × that replaces it. The tooltip reads "Remove from action N". | Remove from Action |
573	| One row | Right-click it and choose **Remove from action N**. | Remove from Action |
574	| A whole section | Click **Clear** in the section's header. Its tooltip reads "Remove this section from action N". | Clear |
575	| Everything | [Remove the action](/motion/change-an-action/#remove-an-action). | Remove Action |
576	
577	### Clear and Reset
578	
579	**Clear** and **Reset** share one place in a section's header, and at most one of them shows.
580	
581	- While an action is selected, a section with rows that can animate shows **Clear** if the action animates anything in it, and neither button if it doesn't.
582	- A section of ⊘ rows keeps **Reset**, because its edits go to the clip.
583	- There, and in any section with no action selected, **Reset** shows only while the section differs from its defaults.
584	
585	## Right-click a row
586	
587	Right-click a row's label, slider, checkbox or the space beside them. Each item shows only where it applies, and a row with nothing to offer has no menu. A text field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click menu.
588	
589	| Item | When it shows | What it does |
590	| --- | --- | --- |
591	| **Remove from action N** | The selected action animates the row | Takes the row out of the action. |
592	| **Go to action M** | The row shows ◇ | Selects the action that animates the row, and moves the playhead to that action's end. |
593	| **Set end value to default** | An action is selected, and the row has a default and can animate | Sets the value at the action's end to the row's default. |
594	| **Reset to default** | Any other row with a default | Puts the row back to its default. |
595	
596	The two default items are greyed while the row already holds its default.
597	
598	**Set end value to default** and **Remove from action N** aren't the same. The first makes the clip animate to the default. The second stops the action touching the row.
599	
600	## Good to know
601	
602	- Typing the number a field already shows isn't an edit, so it doesn't add the row to the action.
603	- Some rows always change the clip, whatever is selected, and they're marked ⊘. [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/) lists them.
604	- Adding or removing a filter or an obscure region changes the clip even inside an action, though dialling a value inside one animates. If the action already animates that list, the whole list then switches at the action's end rather than ramping.
605	- With several clips selected, the fields edit the clips themselves. The action lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions."
606	- An end value Frame Job won't take shows the reason at the foot of the inspector. See [When an edit is refused](/motion/change-an-action/#when-an-edit-is-refused).
607	- Selecting an action isn't an undo step, but each change to its end state is.
608	
609	## With an agent
610	
611	`set_action_end` does what the fields do. It needs the clip, the action and the values to end at, grouped as `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic`, with `speed` beside them. What you send merges into what the action already holds. A key set to `null` takes that property out of the action, and a path listed in `off` switches the property off at the action's end.
612	
613	It can also do one thing the fields can't: send a value past a row's usual range, which is only held to that range as the clip is drawn. There are two exceptions: a graphic's properties are checked when they're set, and a Speed action's rate is held to ×0.1–×1000 when it's set.
614	
615	A few things can't be an action's target, because they belong to the clip: its motion preset (`video.motion`), Hide While Silent (`video.hide_silent`), a text clip's word timing (`text.words`), and a cutout's subject and quality (`video.cutout.subject`, `video.cutout.quality`). Set those with `set_video` or `set_text`. See [`set_action_end`](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).

648	## Move an action
649	
650	Drag the body of a band, on the timeline or in the Clip tab's action lane, to move the action within its clip. The pointer is an open hand over the body, and a dashed outline marks where the band started.
651	
652	When you let go, the action is selected and the playhead sits at its new end, or one frame short of it when the action ends with the clip. The whole drag is one undo step, **Move Action**.
653	
654	## Resize an action
655	
656	Drag either end of a band to move that end of the action. Each end's grip is its outer 5 pt. The grips appear when you hover over the band, and the pointer becomes a left-right arrow over them.
657	
658	The action stays selected and the playhead goes to its new end, as with a move. The whole drag is one undo step, **Resize Action**.
659	
660	A band 15 pt wide or narrower has no grips and only moves. [Zoom the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) in, or type a [length](#type-a-start-length-or-curve).
661	
662	## Where a drag stops
663	
664	A band drag snaps to whole frames and keeps the action at least one frame long. It stops at the neighbouring actions and at the clip's ends. It doesn't snap to the playhead or to other edits.
665	
666	If Frame Job wouldn't allow a position, the band stops there and shows no message. A Speed action stops where the clip would run out of media, for example.
667	
668	An action that a trim left running past the clip's end can move earlier or get shorter, but can't end any later than it already does.
669	
670	On the timeline, a band on a locked track doesn't drag, and clicking it selects the clip, not the action. Select the action in the Clip tab's lane instead.
671	
672	## The drag readout
673	
674	While you drag, a small readout gives the band's new place.
675	
676	| You're dragging | The readout shows | Example |
677	| --- | --- | --- |
678	| The body, or the start grip | The new start, the new end, and how far the start has moved in seconds and frames | `00:00:01:00 → 00:00:03:00  +0:12` |
679	| The end grip | How much the length has changed, in frames | `len −6f` |
680	
681	On the timeline the readout floats above the clip and gives timeline times. In the Clip tab's lane it replaces the header text and gives times from the clip's own start, to match the Start field.
682	
683	## Drag in the Clip tab's lane
684	
685	The lane moves and resizes bands as the timeline does, with the same limits. It differs in three ways:
686	
687	- It selects the action when you let go, where the timeline selects when you press. A click and a drop both select, and both move the playhead to the action's end.
688	- A locked track doesn't stop a click or a drag here.
689	- It shows a zero-length action, which the timeline doesn't draw.
690	
691	## Type a start, length or curve
692	
693	The action lane's detail row shows while an action is selected.
694	
695	| Control | What it does | Limits |
696	| --- | --- | --- |
697	| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode from the clip's own start, not the timeline's. | Capped at the clip's length and snapped to a frame. |
698	| Length | How long the action takes, in seconds, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2. | 0.01 to 36,000 s, then capped at the clip's length and snapped to a frame. |
699	| Curve | How the action eases from its start to its end state. A small glyph of the curve sits beside the pop-up. | **Linear**, **In**, **Out** or **In Out**. |
700	| Trash button | [Removes the action](#remove-an-action). | |
701	
702	**Linear** runs at a constant speed. **In** starts slowly and ends fast, **Out** starts fast and ends slowly, and **In Out** is slow at both ends.
703	
704	Each change is one undo step: **Move Action**, **Resize Action** or **Action Curve**.
705	
706	A Start that isn't a timecode beeps and goes back to the old value. A Length under half a frame rounds to nothing, and Frame Job shows an error alert instead.
707	
708	Length is capped at the whole clip, not at the room left after the action's start, so a long enough value can still run past the clip's end, and Frame Job won't take that. The next section has the reasons it gives.
709	
710	## When an edit is refused
711	
712	If Frame Job won't take a typed Start or Length, or an [end value](/motion/edit-an-action/), it beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused: ". The message stays until the project next changes or you click it. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/) for how to read it.
713	
714	| Frame Job won't do this when | What to do |
715	| --- | --- |
716	| The action would end past the clip's end, and later than it did before | Shorten it or move it earlier. |
717	| The action would overlap another action on the clip | Move or shorten one of them. |
718	| A Speed action would make the clip run out of media | Use the latest clip end the message names. |
719	| The edit would change a Speed action on a clip that's linked to another | Choose **Attach Audio** first, as the message says. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). |
720	
721	A band drag never shows this message. The band stops instead.
722	
723	## Remove an action
724	
725	Select the action, then press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, choose **Edit ▸ Delete**, or click the trash button in the action lane. Only the action goes, as one undo step, **Remove Action**.
726	
727	The clip keeps its own properties and loses what the action did to them.
728	
729	A Speed action can't be removed if the clip would then run out of media. The message names the latest clip end that fits. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/). On a clip that's linked to another, choose **Attach Audio** before you remove a Speed action.
730	
731	## Ripple Delete still deletes the clip
732	
733	:::caution
734	<kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> (**Ripple Delete**) deletes the whole selected clip and closes the gap, even while an action is selected. Only <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the action.
735	:::
736	
737	## Good to know
738	
739	- Moving, resizing or removing a Speed action re-times the captions on a Captions track that sit wholly inside a clip with sound, in the same undo step. The step's name gains "and Re-time Captions". A caption whose speech the clip no longer plays is removed. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
740	- With words selected in the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes those words, not the action.
741	- In the Clip tab's lane, a zero-length action draws as a band 2 pt wide. You can click it to select it, but it doesn't drag. The timeline doesn't draw it at all.
742	- Clicking a band on a clip in a multi-clip selection selects that clip alone.
743	
744	## With an agent
745	
746	`set_action` moves an action, changes its length or changes its curve in one step, and `remove_action` removes it. Both need the clip and the action. Give `set_action` any of `start`, `duration` and `curve`, and what you leave out keeps its value. The curves are `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` and `ease_in_out`.
747	
748	Where a band stops, an agent's edit that goes too far fails, with the same reason a typed value gets. When a Speed action changes or goes, the answer lists the captions it re-timed in `captions_retimed` and those it took out in `captions_removed`. See [`set_action`](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action) and [`remove_action`](/mcp/tools-animation/#remove_action).
749

758	=================== how-edits-move-actions
759	---
760	title: "How edits move actions"
761	description: "See what trimming, splitting, slipping, retiming, copying or freezing a clip does to its actions and its motion presets."
762	---
763	
764	An action's times are measured from the clip's own start, not from the start of the timeline. So moving a clip takes its actions with it, but an edit that changes where the clip starts, how long it is or what it plays can change what an action lands on. This page goes through those edits one at a time, so you know what to expect, and where to look when a zoom no longer lands where you put it.
765	
766	## Trim
767	
768	**Trimming the start** keeps each action's time on the clip. An action 2 s into the clip is still 2 s into the clip afterwards, so it stays put relative to the new start and now plays over different footage.
769	
770	**Trimming the end** leaves actions where they are, so one can end up running past the clip's new end. A start trim shortens the clip too, so it can do the same.
771	
772	Only the part of an action inside the clip plays, so a zoom cut off halfway stops partway in. You can still move that action earlier, shorten it or change its curve, but you can't make it end any later.
773	
774	See [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/).
775	
776	## Slip and roll
777	
778	**Slip** and **Roll** leave actions at the same times on the clip. A slip slides the footage under them. A roll moves the cut between two clips, and the actions on both stay put, as they do for a trim.
779	
780	See [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/).
781	
782	## Speed changes
783	
784	Changing the speed with **Clip ▸ Speed…**, or rate-stretching with an <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag of the end edge, keeps each action at its place as a fraction of the clip. An action a quarter of the way through a clip is still a quarter of the way through, and it gets longer or shorter with the clip. **Clip ▸ Retime Range…** does the same in each clip it changes.
785	
786	The times snap to whole frames, and an action is kept at least one frame long and inside the clip.
787	
788	See [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) and [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/). A clip with a speed ramp has its own rules, in [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
789	
790	## Split
791	
792	**Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>) shares the actions out between the two halves:
793	
794	- An action that ends at or before the cut stays on the first half.
795	- An action that starts at or after the cut goes to the second half, with its times now counted from that half's start.
796	- An action that spans the cut is divided in two. The first piece ends at the values the action had reached at the cut, and the second carries on to the original end state.
797	
798	Both pieces of a divided action keep its curve. The values match at the join, but an eased action can change pace there.
799	
800	## Adding a transition
801	
802	Adding a transition at a hard cut can give the incoming clip a new, earlier first frame, when it has spare footage before the cut. Its actions move with that frame, so a zoom stays on the frame it was drawn over.
803	
804	When there's no spare footage and the incoming clip slides left to make the overlap instead, the clip moves whole and its actions go with it. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).
805	
806	## Duplicate, copy and paste
807	
808	**Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>), an <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag, and **Edit ▸ Copy** then **Paste** all give copies that keep their actions, and the clip's name travels with them. Each copy's actions are its own, so changing one doesn't touch the other.
809	
810	Pasting into a project with a different frame rate snaps the actions' times to that project's frames.
811	
812	See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/) and [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).
813	
814	## Nest
815	
816	Clips you [nest](/editing/nests/) keep their actions inside the nest. Open the nest to see and edit them.
817	
818	## Detach Audio
819	
820	**Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (<kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>) gives the new sound clip a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working. An action that only changes the picture does nothing on the sound clip.
821	
822	## Freeze Frame
823	
824	The still that **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame** (<kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd>) makes has no actions. Instead, the look at the frozen frame is baked into the still's own properties: its position, scale, crop and any other picture setting an action had changed by that moment. So it lines up with the frame it froze, and holds there. See [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/).
825	
826	## Add Blurred Background
827	
828	The backdrop copy that **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes has no actions, so a zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop.
829	
830	## Paste Attributes
831	
832	**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) doesn't copy actions. The clips you paste onto keep the actions they had. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
833	
834	## What keeps or drops motion
835	
836	[Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/) aren't actions, and they follow their own rules.
837	
838	| Edit | What happens to the presets |
839	| --- | --- |
840	| Duplicate, Paste, Detach Audio | Kept. |
841	| Paste Attributes | Copied, with the rest of the clip's picture settings. |
842	| Freeze Frame | The still has none. It sits where the clip sits with no preset applied, so a freeze taken during an entrance can jump. |
843	| Add Blurred Background | The backdrop has none. The foreground keeps its own. |
844	| Split | The first half gives up its Out and the second half its In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. During stays on both halves and restarts at the cut. |
845	| Change the speed | Kept, and not rescaled. |
846	
847	Because During restarts at each cut, [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.
848	
849	## When a graphic's module changes
850	
851	Editing a graphic's [module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#modules) can leave an action animating a property the module no longer has, or no longer lets you animate. With that action selected, the property shows as a dimmed row at the end of **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties**, with its value and a **⌫** button. The tooltip says which of the two happened.
852	
853	Click **⌫** to take the property out of the action. It's one undo step, Remove from Action. An agent does this with `set_action_end`: `graphic.props.<key>: null` takes out one property, and `graphic: null` all of them. See [`set_action_end`](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).
854	
855	See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
856
