864	=================== what-can-animate
865	---
866	title: What an action can animate
867	description: Which properties ramp across an action, which switch at its end, and which can't animate at all, sub-tab by sub-tab.
868	---
869	
870	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
871	
872	An [action](/motion/actions/) can animate most of what's in the Clip tab. This page goes through the tab by sub-tab, so you can see what ramps smoothly, what switches when the action ends, and what can't animate.
873	
874	<AtAGlance
875	  where="Clip tab, with an action selected"
876	  tools="set_action_end"
877	/>
878	
879	With an action selected, the Clip tab marks each row. A row that switches shows "at end" once the action changes it, and most rows that can't animate show ⊘. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for all the marks.
880	
881	One rule applies everywhere. A section you turn on inside an action has no numbers to ramp from, so it appears whole when the action ends. For a gradual start, turn the section on for the clip first and animate its numbers. Turning a section off inside an action turns it off when the action ends.
882	
883	## Picture
884	
885	An action can animate every value in the **Picture** sub-tab, apart from the few under [What never animates](#what-never-animates).
886	
887	| Section | Ramps | Switches at the end |
888	| --- | --- | --- |
889	| [Transform](/canvas/transform/) | **Scale**, **Position X**, **Position Y**, **Rotation**, **Opacity**, [**Motion Blur**](/motion/motion-blur/) | **Blend** |
890	| [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) | | **Behind subject** |
891	| [Crop](/canvas/crop/) | **Left**, **Top**, **Right**, **Bottom** | |
892	| Corner Radius | **Radius** | |
893	| [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/) | **Key Color**, **Tolerance**, **Softness**, **Spill** | **Key out a color** |
894	| [Background](/effects/remove-background/) | **Edge**, **Feather** | **Background** |
895	| [Cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) | **Size**, **Ripple size** | **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks**, **Ripple color** |
896	| [Shadow](/effects/shadow/) | **Color**, **Opacity**, **Blur**, **Angle**, **Distance** | **Drop shadow** |
897	| [Filters](/effects/filters/) | Each filter's **Amount** | A filter's kind |
898	| [Reflection](/effects/reflection/) | **Opacity**, **Height**, **Gap**, **Falloff** | **Mirror the layer below itself** |
899	| [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/) | **Center X**, **Center Y**, **Width**, **Height**, **Feather**, **Dim**, **Zoom** | **Spotlight a region**, **Shape** |
900	| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) | Each region's position, size, **Amount** and **Feather** | A region's kind and **Shape** |
901	
902	Filters and obscure regions follow the [list rule](/motion/actions/#lists). Changing a value inside an existing entry animates, but adding or removing an entry [changes the clip](#what-never-animates).
903	
904	The **Layout** section's **Switch at Playhead** makes actions of its own. See [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/).
905	
906	## Color
907	
908	An action can animate the whole grade in the **Color** sub-tab.
909	
910	| Section | What animates |
911	| --- | --- |
912	| Light | Every slider |
913	| Color | Every slider |
914	| [Wheels](/color/wheels/) | Each wheel and its master strip |
915	| [Curves](/color/curves/) | Every channel, whatever the number of points |
916	| [Look](/color/looks/) | **Amount** |
917	| [Adjustment](/color/adjustment-clips/), on an adjustment clip | **Strength** |
918	| [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/), on an adjustment clip | Each range's numbers. **Invert** and turning a range on or off switch at the end |
919	
920	Choosing a look or a LUT, changing it or removing it changes the clip itself, even with an action selected. Only **Amount** animates. If an agent gives an action a different look, it switches at the end. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
921	
922	## Sound
923	
924	An action can animate the **Sound** sub-tab's **Volume** and **Fades** sections, and every other audio setting apart from the few listed under [What never animates](#what-never-animates). <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking the [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) adds volume actions too.
925	
926	Numbers ramp. Switches change when the action ends: **Mute**, **Mix to mono**, **Channels**, the EQ's slots and slopes, Hum's mains and harmonics, the Leveller's **Response**, and turning a section on or off. Voice Isolation is the exception: **Isolate voice** and **Amount** both ramp from 0 on a clip with none.
927	
928	**Normalize** sets the clip's own level whatever is selected, and its row shows a small "clip" tag while an action is selected.
929	
930	See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
931	
932	## Text
933	
934	An action can animate the **Text** sub-tab's style, size and colours.
935	
936	| Section | Ramps | Switches at the end |
937	| --- | --- | --- |
938	| Content | | The words |
939	| Font | **Size** | **Family**, **Style** |
940	| Style | **Color**, **Line spacing**, **Tracking** | **Align**, **Vertical**, **UPPERCASE** |
941	| Outline | **Width**, **Color** | **Outline** |
942	| Backdrop | **Fill**, **Padding**, **Radius** | **Backdrop** |
943	| Box | **Width** | **Mode** |
944	| Reveal | **In**, **Out** | **Reveal** |
945	
946	Choosing one of the **Presets** with an action selected sets the action's end state, and each value then ramps or switches as above.
947	
948	A word caption page's timing can't animate, because it belongs to the speech. There's no inspector section for its word colours and pop scale, so only an agent can put those in an action. They ramp when it does. See [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
949	
950	For the rows themselves, see [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).
951	
952	## Graphics
953	
954	An action can animate a graphic clip's properties in the **Properties** section of the **Graphic** sub-tab. Numbers and colours ramp, while strings, booleans, choices and images switch at the end. A property the graphic marks as not animatable shows ⊘, and so do the **Size** and **Timeline** sections.
955	
956	See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
957	
958	## Speed
959	
960	An action can change a media clip's playback rate, which makes a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/). With an action selected, **Rate** in the **Clip** sub-tab's **Speed** section sets the rate the action ends at, and the clip holds that rate afterwards.
961	
962	- The rate goes from ×0.1 to ×1000.
963	- The clip keeps its start and length, and plays more or less of its source.
964	- Frame Job won't set a rate that would read past the end of the media, and it names the largest rate that fits.
965	- Above ×12 the clip's sound is left out, and Frame Job asks first. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
966	
967	**Keep pitch** and **Fit to** always change the clip.
968	
969	## What never animates
970	
971	These change the clip itself whatever is selected. Unless the list says otherwise, their rows are marked ⊘ in the Clip tab while an action is selected, and a section where every row is ⊘ says "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip."
972	
973	- **Clip sub-tab:** the [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/) section, and **Keep pitch** and **Fit to** in the Speed section. The Timing and Transition sections change the clip too, and their rows carry no mark.
974	- **Sound sub-tab:** Ducking, the fade shapes (**In shape** and **Out shape**), the Voice Effect, and a nest clip's **Mix to mono**.
975	- **Picture sub-tab:** the [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) section, **Remove background**, **Subject** and the header's **Reset** (which carries no mark) in the Background section, and **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** and **Polish** in the Cursor section.
976	- **Filters and Obscure:** adding or removing a filter or a region. These buttons carry no mark. Changing a value inside an existing entry still animates.
977	- **Shape sub-tab:** a [shape's](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) kind, size, corner radius, stroke, fill, gradient and arrows. These rows carry no mark. Its position, scale and opacity animate like any clip's, through the **Picture** sub-tab. Dragging a shape's handles on the canvas to resize it changes the shape itself.
978	- **Graphic sub-tab:** the **Size** and **Timeline** sections, and any property the graphic marks as not animatable.
979	
980	A track's own volume, pan, compressor and limiter aren't part of a clip, so an action can't reach them.
981	
982	## Colours blend in OKLab
983	
984	Every colour that ramps in an action blends through the OKLab colour space. It keeps the midpoints even and avoids the muddy middle of a straight RGB blend. Pure red to pure blue passes through `#8c53a2` halfway, for example, where a straight RGB blend would give the darker `#800080`.
985	
986	This covers the shadow, chroma key, text, outline, backdrop, word caption and graphic colours. A cursor's **Ripple color** doesn't ramp, and switches at the end. Opacity moves separately from the colour. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact all the way through, and there's no setting for any of this.
987	
988	Shape colours can't animate at all.
989	
990	## With an agent
991	
992	`set_action_end` writes an action's end state. It takes the same keys as `set_video`, `set_audio` and `set_text`, grouped under `video`, `audio` and `text`, with a graphic's properties under `graphic`. A rate goes in `speed`, beside those groups, and `speed: null` takes it back out.
993	
994	Frame Job won't accept the keys that belong to the clip: `video.motion`, `video.hide_silent`, `text.words`, `video.cutout.subject` and `video.cutout.quality`. See [`set_action_end`](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).

1	=================== motion-presets
2	---
3	title: Motion presets
4	description: Give a clip a ready-made entrance, exit or continuous movement that's tied to its two ends and stays with it through a trim.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	A motion preset says what a clip does rather than where it is: how it arrives, how it leaves and what it does in between. It's tied to the clip's two ends, so it goes with the clip through a trim and there's nothing to reposition afterwards.
11	
12	Each clip has three slots, and all three can run on the same clip:
13	
14	- **In** is an entrance at the clip's start: Fade, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Slide Left, Slide Right, Slide Up, Slide Down, Spin or Pop. See [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/).
15	- **Out** is an exit at the clip's end, from the same nine kinds.
16	- **During** is a movement for the clip's whole length: Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce or Drift. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).
17	
18	Presets work on any clip that draws a picture: video, still images, text, shapes, graphics and nests.
19	
20	<AtAGlance
21	  menu={['Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Out', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview']}
22	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
23	  tools="set_video"
24	/>
25	
26	## Give a clip a preset
27	
28	<Steps>
29	
30	1. Select the clip.
31	
32	2. In the Clip tab, pick the **Clip** sub-tab and open **Motion presets**, the last section. It's closed by default.
33	
34	3. Choose a kind from **In**, **Out** or **During**.
35	
36	4. Set **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or for a During movement, **Amount** and **Period**.
37	
38	5. Choose **Preview** to watch it loop.
39	
40	</Steps>
41	
42	If the defaults suit you, [the Motion menu](#use-the-motion-menu) is quicker.
43	
44	## The Motion presets section
45	
46	| Row | What it does | Range | Default |
47	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
48	| **In** | How the clip enters. | None and nine kinds | None |
49	| **In Duration** | How long the entrance takes. Dimmed while **In** is None. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 | 0.5 s |
50	| **Out** | How the clip leaves. | None and nine kinds | None |
51	| **Out Duration** | How long the exit takes. Dimmed while **Out** is None. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 | 0.5 s |
52	| **During** | What the clip does for its whole length. | None and five kinds | None |
53	| **Amount** | How strong the During movement is. Dimmed while **During** is None. | 0 to 100%, with quick picks of 25, 50, 75 and 100 | 50% |
54	| **Period** | How long one cycle of the During movement takes. Dimmed while **During** is None, and for Drift, which has no cycle. | 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 | 1 s |
55	| **Preview** | Loops the clip so you can [watch its motion](#preview-a-preset). | | |
56	
57	The two durations and **Period** snap to the project's frame grid. The In is measured from the clip's first frame and the Out back from its last.
58	
59	The section's header sums up the first selected clip's presets, for example "in fade · out slide left · pulse". With no presets it reads "off".
60	
61	## Use the Motion menu
62	
63	**Clip ▸ Motion** has three submenus, **In**, **Out** and **During**, then [**Preview**](#preview-a-preset). Each submenu lists its kinds, then **None** to clear the slot. They work on every selected clip that has a picture, and they're dimmed when no selected clip has one. None of them has a keyboard shortcut.
64	
65	A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares. If the clips disagree, nothing is checked. If none of them has a preset in that slot, **None** is checked. A kind can also carry an [(inactive)](#inactive-presets) label.
66	
67	## Change or clear a preset
68	
69	Choosing a different kind keeps the settings the slot already had: an In or Out keeps its duration, and a During keeps its amount and period. A slot that's empty, including one you've set to **None**, starts at the defaults: 0.5 s for an In or Out, and 50% with a 1 s period for a During.
70	
71	To clear one slot, choose **None**. To clear all three, choose **Reset** in the section's header. **Reset** shows only when the first selected clip has a preset, and it clears every selected clip.
72	
73	Each change is one undo step, however many clips are selected.
74	
75	## Set presets on several clips
76	
77	With several clips selected, a change to one slot leaves each clip's other slots as they were. Choosing a new In kind doesn't touch anyone's Out, and each clip keeps its own In duration.
78	
79	The section shows the first selected clip's values, with **mixed** beside a row where the clips differ. That has two effects to watch for:
80	
81	- **In Duration**, **Out Duration**, **Amount** and **Period** only change the clips that have a preset in that slot. The others are left alone.
82	- Those rows are dimmed by the first clip alone. If the first selected clip has no In, **In Duration** is dimmed even when other selected clips have one.
83	
84	## Preview a preset
85	
86	Choose **Preview** in the section, or **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview**. Frame Job sets the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) to the clip, turns [Loop](/timeline/loop/) on, moves the playhead to the clip's start and plays.
87	
88	With several clips selected, it loops the first selected clip that has a picture.
89	
90	The range and Loop stay until you clear them. Choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range** (<kbd>⌥X</kbd>) and click the **Loop** button in the toolbar. A range you'd already set is replaced.
91	
92	## Read presets on the timeline
93	
94	Small marks on a clip's name strip show its presets:
95	
96	- **A wedge at each end** along the bottom of the strip stands for an In or an Out. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, at least 2 points wide so a short preset still shows, and never wider than the clip. The Clip tab's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) shows the same two wedges, hanging from its top.
97	- **A wave symbol** at the right end of the strip stands for a During movement. On a clip too narrow to fit it, the symbol is left out.
98	
99	See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) for everything else a clip draws.
100	
101	## Motion sits on top of placement
102	
103	A preset works relative to the clip. Frame Job takes the clip's own placement and any [actions](/motion/actions/) first, then applies the preset on top:
104	
105	- Its scale and opacity multiply the clip's own. A clip at 50% opacity fades in to 50%, not 100%.
106	- Its rotation and offset add to the clip's own.
107	- Anything that changes the clip's size or turns it does so about the clip's visible centre, after any crop.
108	- The drawn size stays within the 1% to 1,000% that **Scale** allows.
109	
110	The three slots add up the same way, so a clip can slide in while it pulses.
111	
112	### The inspector shows un-moved values
113	
114	The fields in the Clip tab show the clip's own numbers, even while the preview and the export show it moving. Halfway through a Zoom In, **Scale** still reads what you typed. That's why editing a clip's position or size works the same with a preset on it.
115	
116	### Dragging during motion
117	
118	A drag on the canvas changes the clip's own position, starting from where it sits without the preset. If you drag partway through a preset, the distance you drag is added to that un-moved position, and the preset keeps playing on top of it. To place a clip by eye, park the playhead where its In has finished and its Out hasn't started.
119	
120	## Overlong presets shorten
121	
122	An In and an Out can together last longer than the clip. Frame Job keeps both and shortens them in proportion to their lengths, so the entrance ends on the frame where the exit begins. A 2 s In and a 1 s Out on a 1.5 s clip play as 1 s and 0.5 s. An In or Out alone that's longer than the clip plays over the clip's whole length.
123	
124	On the timeline the wedges aren't shortened, so they overlap. That's how to spot it. **In Duration** and **Out Duration** keep what you set too, so if you lengthen the clip later, the presets get their full time back.
125	
126	## Inactive presets
127	
128	An In or Out with a zero duration can come from an agent. Frame Job keeps it but it does nothing, and it draws no wedge. It's marked so you can fix it:
129	
130	- The section's summary reads, for example, "in fade (inactive)".
131	- The **Clip ▸ Motion** submenus read **Fade (inactive)**, or **Fade (some inactive)** when only some of the selected clips with that kind have a zero duration.
132	- A note at the top of the section reads "Selection includes inactive In motion (zero duration). Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear." It names **In**, **Out** or **In and Out**, and it counts every selected clip.
133	
134	Changing the kind doesn't fix it, because a new kind keeps the old duration. Raise **In Duration** or **Out Duration**, or choose **None**.
135	
136	## Presets and actions
137	
138	An [action](/motion/actions/) animates a property to a value you set, over a span you place on the clip. A preset is anchored to the clip's ends and says what the clip does. Use a preset for an entrance, an exit or a repeating movement, and an action when a value has to reach a particular number at a particular moment.
139	
140	A preset is never part of an action, and no action can animate one. While an action is selected, the section's rows are marked ⊘ and the section reads "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." Your edits there write the clip, as they do with no action selected, and **Reset** is still available.
141	
142	## How edits treat a preset
143	
144	| Edit | What happens to the presets |
145	| --- | --- |
146	| Trim | Each preset moves with its edge and keeps its length. |
147	| [Split](/editing/splitting/) | The first half keeps the In and gives up the Out, and the second half keeps the Out and gives up the In, so the cut doesn't play an exit and an entrance. Both halves keep the During. |
148	| [Change the speed](/speed/change-speed/) | The presets aren't rescaled. A 0.5 s In stays 0.5 s, and a clip that gets much shorter can make its presets [shorten](#overlong-presets-shorten). |
149	| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still has no preset, and it sits at the clip's un-moved position, so a freeze taken mid-motion can jump. |
150	| [Add Blurred Background](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) | The backdrop copy doesn't move. The clip in front keeps its presets. |
151	| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and [Paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | The presets are kept. |
152	| [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) | Presets are copied with the rest of the picture settings. |
153	
154	A During movement restarts at each cut, because each piece is a clip of its own. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at the cuts.
155	
156	## Good to know
157	
158	- A preset moves the picture only. A Fade leaves the sound as it is, so use [audio fades](/audio/fades/) for that.
159	- A preset on a [nest](/editing/nests/) moves everything inside the nest together.
160	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) have the section and draw the marks, but there's no picture to move. Only a preset's fade has an effect, and it fades the clip's strength.
161	- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) blurs a preset's movement like any other.
162	- [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) works out its zoom without a During movement, and tells you so with "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it".
163	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) works on an upright picture, so it won't take a clip with Spin in any slot.
164	- Changing the project's frame rate moves the durations and the period onto the new frame grid.
165	
166	## With an agent
167	
168	An agent sets and clears presets with the `motion` key of `set_video`, which is `null` or `{in, out, during}`. `in` and `out` each take a `kind` and a `duration`. `during` takes a `kind`, an `amount` from 0 to 1 and a `period`, and Drift ignores its period. Durations and periods are written in [an agent's time units](/mcp/units-and-ids/#times-in-ticks).
169	
170	A slot left out keeps what it had, a slot set to `null` is cleared, and `{motion: null}` clears all three.
171	
172	An agent isn't held to the section's ranges. Any duration of zero or more is accepted, which is how an [inactive preset](#inactive-presets) comes about, and a period can be outside 0.1 to 10 s as long as it's above zero. Frame Job won't accept an amount outside 0 to 1, which is 0 to 100%. Durations and periods snap to the frame grid, so the value read back can differ a little from the one sent.
173	
174	`get_project` reports the clip's un-moved values, so use `render_frame` to see a preset's effect. `set_action_end` won't take a preset, not even to clear one. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#motion) for the full list of keys, and [Entrance and exit presets](/motion/entrances-and-exits/#with-an-agent) for the values of `kind`.

189	---

192	
193	Entrance and exit presets give a clip a ready-made way to arrive and to leave. The same nine kinds fill a clip's **In** and **Out** slots, and each runs for the **In Duration** or **Out Duration** you set, 0.5 s unless you change it. This page says what each kind does at each end. To set one, see [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).
194	
195	<AtAGlance
196	  menu={['Clip ▸ Motion ▸ In', 'Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Out']}
197	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
198	  tools="set_video"

200	
201	## How In and Out relate
202	
203	An In and an Out of the same kind are a pair, not a rewind: a Zoom In grows at both ends and a Slide Left travels left at both ends. An In starts quickly and slows as the clip arrives. An Out starts slowly and speeds up as the clip leaves. Pop is the exception, because it has a spring of its own.
204	
205	Sizes here are relative to the clip's own size, and fades to its own opacity. A clip placed at 50% scale that zooms in from 60% starts at 30%. See [Motion sits on top of placement](/motion/motion-presets/#motion-sits-on-top-of-placement).
206	
207	## Fade
208	
209	The clip's opacity changes and nothing else does.
210	
211	- **As an In:** fades in from fully transparent.
212	- **As an Out:** fades out.
213	
214	## Zoom In
215	
216	The clip grows, whichever end it's at.
217	
218	- **As an In:** grows from 60% to full size while fading in.
219	- **As an Out:** grows to 140% while fading out.
220	
221	## Zoom Out
222	
223	The clip shrinks, whichever end it's at.
224	
225	- **As an In:** shrinks from 140% to full size while fading in.
226	- **As an Out:** shrinks to 60% while fading out.
227	
228	## Slide Left
229	
230	A slide names the direction the clip travels. It doesn't fade, so the clip stays at its own opacity the whole way. This one travels left.
231	
232	- **As an In:** slides in from the right edge.
233	- **As an Out:** slides out past the left edge.
234	
235	## Slide Right
236	
237	The clip travels right, with no fade.
238	
239	- **As an In:** slides in from the left edge.
240	- **As an Out:** slides out past the right edge.
241	
242	## Slide Up
243	
244	The clip travels up, with no fade.
245	
246	- **As an In:** slides in from the bottom edge.
247	- **As an Out:** slides out past the top edge.
248	
249	## Slide Down
250	
251	The clip travels down, with no fade.
252	
253	- **As an In:** slides in from the top edge.
254	- **As an Out:** slides out past the bottom edge.
255	
256	## Spin
257	
258	The clip makes half a turn, clockwise at both ends.
259	
260	- **As an In:** spins half a turn into place, growing from 30% size and fading in.
261	- **As an Out:** spins half a turn away, shrinking to 30% size and fading out.
262	
263	## Pop
264	
265	The clip springs past full size, so it overshoots where the others stop.
266	
267	- **As an In:** grows from nothing, overshoots to about 110% and settles at full size. It fades in over the first quarter of its duration.
268	- **As an Out:** swells to about 110%, then shrinks to nothing. It fades out over the last quarter.
269	
270	## How slides measure
271	
272	A slide measures the clip as it's drawn, with its scale, rotation and crop, from wherever you've placed it. So it starts or ends exactly off the edge of the canvas, however large the clip is and wherever it sits.
273	
274	Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), that edge is the nest's own canvas rather than the project's.
275	
276	## Slides on text
277	
278	A text clip has no measured size, so a slide can't work out exactly where it leaves the canvas. It starts or ends half a canvas past the edge instead. That clears any text narrower than the canvas. Text wider than the canvas can still show at the start of a slide in or the end of a slide out.
279	
280	## Good to know
281	
282	- An Out finishes at the end of the clip's last frame, not on it, so that frame still shows a sliver of the clip. A Fade isn't quite fully transparent there.
283	- Every kind works with every During movement, so a clip can slide in while it pulses. See [During presets](/motion/during-presets/).
284	- A preset only moves the picture. For sound, see [Audio fades](/audio/fades/).
285	
286	## With an agent
287	
288	An agent names a kind in the `motion` key of `set_video`: `fade`, `zoom_in`, `zoom_out`, `slide_left`, `slide_right`, `slide_up`, `slide_down`, `spin` or `pop`. An `in` is measured from the clip's first frame and an `out` back from its last. See [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/#with-an-agent) and [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#motion).

298	title: During presets
299	description: Give a clip a movement that runs all the way through it, such as a pulse, a shake or a slow push-in, and set how strong and how fast it is.
300	---
301	
302	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
303	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
304	
305	A During preset is a movement that runs for a clip's whole length: a gentle pulse, a shake, a spin, a hop or a slow push-in. It's one of a clip's three [motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/), beside [In and Out](/motion/entrances-and-exits/), and it works on any clip that draws a picture: video, stills, text, shapes, graphics and nests.
306	
307	<AtAGlance
308	  menu="Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During"
309	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Motion presets"
310	  tools="set_video"
311	/>
312	
313	## Add a During movement
314	
315	<Steps>
316	
317	1. Select one or more clips.
318	
319	2. On the Clip tab's **Clip** sub-tab, open the **Motion presets** section.
320	
321	3. Choose a kind from **During**: Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce or Drift. It starts at half strength with a one-second cycle.
322	
323	4. Set [Amount](#amount) and [Period](#period).
324	
325	5. Choose **Preview** to watch it loop. Preview sets the in/out range to the clip, turns Loop on and plays, and both stay until you clear them.
326	
327	</Steps>
328	
329	**Clip ▸ Motion ▸ During** sets the kind too. A checkmark shows the kind every selected clip shares, and there's no checkmark when they differ. The menu is dimmed with nothing selected, or when every selected clip comes from a sound-only file.
330	
331	To take the movement off, choose **None** in the row or in the menu. Switching straight from one kind to another keeps the Amount and Period you set, but going through **None** clears them, so the next kind starts at 50% and 1 s.
332	
333	A clip with a During movement shows a small wave symbol at the right end of its name strip, when the strip has room.
334	
335	With several clips selected, a new kind goes to every clip that draws a picture, and each clip keeps its own In and Out. **Amount** and **Period** change only the selected clips that already have a During movement. Each change is one undo step, however many clips it touches.
336	
337	## The movements
338	
339	Every kind is described at 100% and at the default 50%. [Amount](#amount) scales between them, and 0% is no movement.
340	
341	### Pulse
342	
343	The clip gently grows and shrinks, once per Period. It starts at its own size, is largest halfway through the cycle, and is back at its own size at the end. At 100% it grows to 20% larger, and at 50% to 10% larger.
344	
345	### Shake
346	
347	The clip jitters in every direction, in a pattern that never visibly repeats. At 100% it moves up to 4% of the canvas's shorter edge on each axis, and at 50% up to 2%. A shorter Period shakes faster.
348	
349	### Spin
350	
351	The clip turns clockwise without stopping. At 50% it makes one full turn per Period, at 100% two turns, and at 25% half a turn.
352	
353	### Bounce
354	
355	The clip hops upward once per Period and lands back where it started. At 100% each hop is up to 8% of the canvas height, and at 50% up to 4%.
356	
357	### Drift
358	
359	A slow push-in across the whole clip. The clip grows steadily from its own size and ends 24% larger at 100%, or 12% larger at 50%.
360	
361	Drift ignores Period. Its speed comes from the clip's length, so a longer clip reaches the same size more slowly.
362	
363	## Amount
364	
365	How strong the movement is, from 0 to 100%, with quick picks at 25, 50, 75 and 100. The default is 50%. A number outside the range is brought back to the nearest end.
366	
367	At 0% the clip stays still but keeps its During kind. **Amount** is greyed while **During** is **None**.
368	
369	## Period
370	
371	How long one cycle takes, from 0.1 to 10 s, with quick picks at 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2. The default is 1 s, and what you type lands on the nearest frame.
372	
373	**Period** is greyed while **During** is **None**, and for Drift. Drift keeps the value, so it's still there if you switch to another kind.
374	
375	## How During starts
376	
377	Every During movement starts from the clip's own placement on its first frame. The clip begins exactly where you put it, whatever it goes on to do.
378	
379	The movement sits on top of that placement and of any [actions](/motion/actions/). Its size multiplies the clip's own scale, and its turn and offset add to the clip's own rotation and position. Pulse, Spin and Drift work around the clip's visible centre, after any crop.
380	
381	The inspector still shows the clip's own values, not the moved ones, even though the preview and the export show it moving.
382	
383	## During with In and Out
384	
385	A During movement runs under the In and Out, so a clip can slide in while it pulses. Their sizes multiply, and their turns and offsets add, so a Spin entrance and a During Spin turn together.
386	
387	A During movement never changes a clip's opacity. Only In and Out fade a clip.
388	
389	## During restarts at a cut
390	
391	A During movement counts from each clip's own first frame, so cutting a clip restarts it. After a [split](/editing/splitting/), both halves keep the movement and the second half starts over.
392	
393	That can show as a jump at the cut. A Pulse goes back to the start of its cycle, and a Drift drops back to the clip's own size and drifts again across the shorter piece. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) on a clip with Pulse or Drift can make it jump at every cut.
394	
395	To keep one movement going across cuts, [nest](/editing/nests/) the pieces and give the nest clip the During movement.
396	
397	## Good to know
398	
399	- A preset is not part of any [action](/motion/what-can-animate/). With an action selected, the **Motion presets** rows are marked ⊘ and still edit the clip, so **Amount** can't ramp.
400	- Changing a clip's speed doesn't change its During movement. **Period** stays the same length on the timeline, and a Drift spreads over the clip's new length.
401	- Inside a nest, Shake and Bounce measure against the nest's canvas, not the project's.
402	- A Pulse or Drift can't draw a clip past 1,000%, the largest scale a clip can have.
403	- Freeze Frame and Add Blurred Background leave the movement behind. Duplicate, Detach Audio and Paste keep it.
404	- A drag on the canvas that starts while the clip is moving starts from the clip's own position, not the moved one.
405	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) won't frame a clip with a Spin, whether it's the In, the Out or the During, because it needs an upright picture.
406	- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) counts a During movement as motion.
407	
408	## With an agent
409	
410	An agent sets During through `set_video`, with a `kind` of `pulse`, `shake`, `spin`, `bounce` or `drift`, an `amount` from 0 to 1, and a `period`.
411	
412	An agent isn't held to the row's range for Period. A period shorter than one frame becomes one frame. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#motion).

429	Motion blur streaks a moving clip along the way it moved during each frame, as a camera's shutter would. It takes the hard steps out of a fast zoom, pan or slide.

436	## Add motion blur
437	
438	<Steps>
439	
440	1. Select a clip that moves.
441	
442	2. On the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, open **Transform**.
443	
444	3. Raise **Motion Blur** above 0%.
445	
446	</Steps>
447	
448	**Motion Blur** runs from 0 to 100%, with quick picks at 0, 25, 50 and 100. It's off by default.
449	
450	The number is the share of one frame the shutter stays open for. 50% is a film camera's 180° shutter, so it's a good place to start. At 100% the clip streaks along everything it moved in that frame.
451	
452	The blur shows when the clip moves:
453	
454	- A zoom or pan in an [action](/motion/actions/).
455	- A [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/).
456	- The [nest](/editing/nests/) it sits in moving.
457	
458	A clip's [recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) streaks along its own path too, even when the clip stands still. The cursor's click ripples stay sharp.
459	
460	The Transform section's **Reset** puts **Motion Blur** back to 0% with the section's other rows.
461	
462	[Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/) has a **Motion blur** box of its own. Ticked, it sets 50% on the clips it zooms, unless they already have a blur.
463	
464	## How it is drawn
465	
466	The blur is the same in the preview, in [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/), in every export and in a frame an agent renders. Each frame draws the clip 16 times at its positions across the shutter and averages them. The shutter is centred on the frame.
467	
468	A clip that doesn't move in a frame draws exactly as it does with the blur off, so a clip that moves for only part of its length blurs only while it moves.
469	
470	## Ramp the blur in and out
471	
472	**Motion Blur** can change inside an action, so a blur can build up and fall away.
473	
474	<Steps>
475	
476	1. [Select the action](/motion/select-an-action/).
477	
478	2. Set **Motion Blur**. With an action selected, the row sets the value the action ends on.
479	
480	</Steps>
481	
482	The blur moves from where it stood when the action began to the new value, along the action's curve. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
483	
484	## With blend modes
485	
486	A clip with a [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/) blends its averaged picture once. A screened clip, for example, screens its blurred picture over what's under it.
487	
488	## Where it stays sharp
489	
490	These draw sharp whatever **Motion Blur** says, and the row keeps its value:
491	
492	- A clip in a [transition](/motion/transitions/), for the frames of the overlap, and every clip inside a nest clip that's in one.
493	- A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), and the clips a matte cuts.
494	- A clip cut by [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), and the copy of the person it draws.
495	- A clip with a [drop shadow](/effects/shadow/).
496	- A nest clip itself. The blur goes on the clips inside it. See [Nests and adjustment clips](#nests-and-adjustment-clips).
497	
498	## Nests and adjustment clips
499	
500	A nest clip can't take motion blur, so the row is greyed for it, and for any selection with a nest clip in it. Set the blur on the clips inside the nest instead. They blur when the nest moves.
501	
502	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no picture to move. It has no **Picture** sub-tab, so there's no row to set.
503	
504	## With an agent
505	
506	An agent sets the blur with `motion_blur` in `set_video`, from 0 to 1. 0 is off and the default, and 0.5 is the row's 50%. `set_action_end` sets the value an action ends on, and `render_frame` draws the blur as an export would.
507	
508	On a nest clip or an adjustment clip, a value above 0 stops with an error and 0 always goes through. A nest clip's error reads "clip N shows a nest and cannot take motion blur: set it on the clips inside". See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#motion_blur).
509

518	=================== zoom-to-region
519	---
520	title: "Zoom to Region"
521	description: "Draw a rectangle on the picture to zoom a clip to it, then pull back out with Zoom Back."
522	---
523	
524	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
525	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
526	
527	Zoom to Region is the screencast zoom: draw a rectangle on the picture, and the clip zooms until that rectangle fills the frame. The zoom is an ordinary [action](/motion/actions/), so you can retime it, change its curve or remove it like any other.
528	
529	<AtAGlance
530	  keys="Z"
531	  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane ▸ zoom-in magnifier (Zoom to Region)', 'Clip tab ▸ action lane ▸ zoom-out magnifier (Zoom Back)']}
532	  tools="add_zoom_action"
533	/>
534	
535	## Draw a zoom
536	
537	<Steps>
538	
539	1. Select one clip and put the playhead where the zoom should start.
540	
541	2. Press <kbd>Z</kbd>, or click the zoom-in magnifier in the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). The pointer becomes a crosshair and a hint appears on the canvas.
542	
543	3. Drag a rectangle over the canvas. It can start outside the picture, which helps when you want to catch the edge of the frame.
544	
545	4. Release the mouse.
546	
547	</Steps>
548	
549	Frame Job adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead, shown as **In Out** in the lane's Curve pop-up. Its end state is the scale and position that bring the rectangle to the canvas, allowing for the clip's rotation and crop at that moment. It's one undo step, Zoom to Region.
550	
551	The new action is selected, so you can go straight on to change its length or curve in the lane's [detail row](/motion/action-lane/#detail-row), or adjust where it ends with the [Clip tab's fields or the canvas](/motion/edit-an-action/).
552	
553	The clip stays zoomed after the action ends, until a later action changes it. [Zoom Back](#zoom-back) is the way to pull out again.
554	
555	## The canvas hint and outline
556	
557	While the mode is on, a hint at the top of the canvas reads "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel".
558	
559	As you drag, you see two outlines: the rectangle you're drawing, and a dimmer dashed one showing exactly what the canvas will show once the zoom lands. They differ when your rectangle isn't the shape of the canvas.
560	
561	## Fit or fill
562	
563	| To | Do this | Result |
564	| --- | --- | --- |
565	| Fit | Drag | The whole rectangle is shown. This is the default. |
566	| Fill | Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> while dragging | The rectangle fills the canvas, and whatever doesn't match the canvas shape is cropped. |
567	
568	Frame Job reads <kbd>⇧</kbd> at every step of the drag, so you can change your mind before you let go, and the dashed outline follows.
569	
570	A zoom changes a clip's scale and position, never its angle. On a rotated clip, fit and fill both allow for the rotation, and the dashed outline shows the result.
571	
572	## Zoom Back
573	
574	Zoom Back pulls the clip back out after a zoom.
575	
576	<Steps>
577	
578	1. Move the playhead past the end of the zoom, to where the pull-back should start. After Zoom to Region the playhead is still at the zoom's start, and a new action there would overlap it.
579	
580	2. Click the zoom-out magnifier in the action lane.
581	
582	</Steps>
583	
584	Frame Job adds a 1-second **Ease In Out** action at the playhead whose end state is the clip's own scale, x and y, the values it has outside any action, whatever earlier actions did. There's no rectangle to draw and no key for it. The new action is selected, and it's one undo step, Zoom Back.
585	
586	Like <kbd>Z</kbd>, it beeps when there's no clip it can work on. See [Which clip can be zoomed](#which-clip-can-be-zoomed).
587	
588	## Which clip can be zoomed
589	
590	<kbd>Z</kbd> and Zoom Back need exactly one selected clip that's in the picture at the playhead and isn't on a locked track. Otherwise they beep. So they won't work with several clips selected, with the playhead off the clip, or on a sound-only clip.
591	
592	The action also has to fit. Frame Job won't add a zoom that would overlap another action on the clip or run past the clip's end. It beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector. If you'd drawn a rectangle the mode closes too, so press <kbd>Z</kbd> to try again. Near the end of a clip, move the playhead back first. If another action is in the way, shorten it or move the playhead clear of it.
593	
594	## Leaving the mode
595	
596	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, press <kbd>Z</kbd> again, or click the zoom-in magnifier again. The mode also closes by itself when the selection changes or the playhead leaves the clip, and turning on another canvas tool, such as an eyedropper, ends it.
597	
598	Once focus has left the canvas, for example after a click in the inspector, <kbd>Esc</kbd> no longer reaches the mode, and <kbd>Z</kbd> is the way out.
599	
600	A rectangle under 6 canvas pixels wide or high, or a click with no drag, beeps and leaves the mode on so you can draw again.
601	
602	## The scale limit
603	
604	The zoom stops at 1,000%, the largest scale a layer can take. The rectangle stays centred even then, but it doesn't reach the size you asked for. On a 1920-wide canvas, for example, a rectangle narrower than 192 pixels of the source picture can't fill the width.
605	
606	## With a During preset
607	
608	On a clip with a During [motion preset](/motion/during-presets/), a second hint appears under the first: "This clip has During motion — the zoom is solved without it". The zoom is worked out as if the preset weren't there, and the preset keeps moving the clip under the zoom, so the rectangle won't sit exactly in place.
609	
610	The hint follows the clip, so it appears or goes if a During preset is added or cleared while the mode is on.
611	
612	## Auto Zoom
613	
614	To zoom a screen recording at every click at once, use **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. It plans these same zoom actions from the recording's cursor file. See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/).
615	
616	## Good to know
617	
618	- You draw on the picture as it is at the playhead, with earlier actions applied, so you can draw a tighter zoom on a clip that's already zoomed.
619	- The rotation and crop are read at the start of the zoom. If you then animate either of them in the same action, the rectangle drifts across the action's span.
620	
621	## With an agent
622	
623	An agent gives the rectangle as numbers with `add_zoom_action` instead of drawing it, and can set the zoom's length and curve in the same call. A `region` of `null` is a Zoom Back, and it has to be sent, so a forgotten rectangle can't turn into one. On a clip with no picture the call fails. See [`add_zoom_action`](/mcp/tools-animation/#add_zoom_action).
624

632	=================== transitions
633	---
634	title: Transitions
635	description: How a transition works in Frame Job, as the overlap between two clips on a track, and the rules that decide where one can go.
636	---
637	
638	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
639	
640	A transition carries the picture and sound from one clip into the next. In Frame Job it isn't a separate object you drop on a cut. It's what plays wherever two clips on the same track overlap.
641	
642	<AtAGlance
643	  menu="Clip ▸ Transition ▸"
644	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition"
645	  tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_style', 'set_transition_duration']}
646	/>
647	
648	## What a transition is
649	
650	A transition plays across the overlap between two clips on the same track, and the overlap's length is the transition's duration. To make a transition longer, you make the overlap longer, by dragging or trimming a clip or by typing a [Duration](/motion/transition-settings/#duration).
651	
652	The later clip carries the transition: it's the transition into that clip, and it's stored with that clip. To change one, select the clip that comes second.
653	
654	There are thirteen [styles](/motion/transition-styles/), from Cross Dissolve to pushes, wipes and a zoom. [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) has the ways to make one, and [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/) has its settings.
655	
656	Two clips on different tracks don't transition, however they line up. They're layers, and the front one draws over the back one.
657	
658	## Overlap two clips
659	
660	The quickest transition is an overlap. When an edit leaves a clip overlapping the clip before it on the same track, and the later clip has no transition stored, Frame Job adds a Cross Dissolve. It's eased (**Ease In Out**) and crossfades the sound (**Crossfade Audio** on).
661	
662	That holds however the overlap came about:
663	
664	- Dragging a clip onto its neighbour, or trimming an edge past it.
665	- A duplicate, a paste or an insert.
666	- A ripple delete, a [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) or [Shift Clips Left](/motion/add-a-transition/#shift-clips-left).
667	- A nest or an un-nest.
668	
669	A clip that already has a transition stored keeps it.
670	
671	## The overlap rules
672	
673	Two clips on a track may overlap only as a transition, and two rules limit how:
674	
675	- A clip can overlap at most one neighbour on each side.
676	- An overlap can be at most half as long as the shorter of the two clips. A 4 s clip and a 10 s clip can overlap by up to 2 s.
677	
678	Clips never push each other out of the way, so Frame Job won't make a move, trim, nudge, duplicate, gap close or nest that breaks either rule. A drag stops at the last place that fits, and anything else beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.
679	
680	Two edits work differently:
681	
682	- **Paste and Un-nest** put a clip that would break the rule on a new track at the front.
683	- **A ripple delete** is never stopped by these rules. A clip it slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve.
684	
685	See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule).
686	
687	## On the timeline
688	
689	The overlap draws as a hatched zone across the cut, with a solid edge down each side. The transition's name sits in the zone when the whole word fits. On a short transition the name is left out, and the [Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/) still shows it.
690	
691	See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/#the-transition-zone).
692	
693	## An overlap with no stored transition
694	
695	Choosing **None** removes a stored transition but not the overlap. While the two clips overlap they keep blending, as a linear cross dissolve with no sound crossfade: both clips play at their own level across the overlap. The timeline draws no hatched zone for it.
696	
697	The Transition section says what's there. Its summary reads "none", and it shows **Linear** and **Crossfade Audio** off. Setting either one stores a Cross Dissolve with exactly the values shown, plus your change.
698	
699	This lasts until the next move, trim or other edit that repositions clips on that track, which gives the overlap the usual eased Cross Dissolve. To get a hard cut back, move or trim the clips so they no longer overlap.
700	
701	## A transition needs an overlap
702	
703	A transition stored on a clip that overlaps nothing does nothing until there's an overlap. Drag two clips apart and the later one keeps its transition, with no zone on the timeline. Overlap them again and the same style comes back.
704	
705	The Transition section only appears for a single selected clip that overlaps the clip before it. To clear a stored transition with no overlap, select the clip and choose **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ None**, which is available for any selection.
706	
707	## Clips that can't take a transition
708	
709	[Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't take a transition, so Frame Job won't make a move, trim or other edit that overlaps an adjustment clip with another clip. Fade one with opacity instead.
710	
711	The first clip on a track and a clip after a gap have nothing to overlap, so [the Transition menu skips them](/motion/add-a-transition/#clips-that-are-skipped).
712	
713	## Good to know
714	
715	- Two overlapping clips with no picture get a transition too. Only their sound changes, so the [crossfade settings](/motion/transition-settings/) matter and the style doesn't show.
716	- After [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/), **Crossfade Audio** on the video clips' transition has no effect, because their own sound is off. To crossfade the sound, overlap the detached audio clips and give them a transition of their own.
717	- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) never cut into a transition's overlap.
718	- A clip always blends normally while it's in a transition, whatever [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/) it has.
719	- A clip draws without [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) for the frames of a transition.
720	
721	## With an agent
722	
723	`add_transition` makes an overlap at a hard cut. `set_transition` sets or clears the style, `set_transition_style` sets its curve and crossfade, and `set_transition_duration` changes the length of an overlap. A `move_clip` that makes an overlap gets the same Cross Dissolve as a drag. See [Tools: transitions](/mcp/tools-transitions/).
724	
725	## Related

732	=================== add-a-transition
733	---
734	title: "Add or remove a transition"
735	description: "Put a transition on a cut, change the style of one you already have, get past a cut with no spare footage, and take a transition off again."
736	---
737	
738	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
739	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
740	
741	A transition plays across an overlap between two clips on the same track. **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** makes that overlap for you at a cut, restyles one that's already there, and takes a transition off.
742	
743	<AtAGlance
744	  menu="Clip ▸ Transition ▸"
745	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition ▸ Kind"
746	  tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition']}
747	/>
748	
749	## Add a transition
750	
751	<Steps>
752	
753	1. Select the clip after the cut. A transition belongs to the clip it leads into. To do several cuts at once, select the clip after each cut.
754	
755	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** and a [style](/motion/transition-styles/).
756	
757	</Steps>
758	
759	The overlap appears on the timeline as a hatched zone, with the style's name in it when the word fits. To change its length or easing, use [the Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
760	
761	## The Transition menu
762	
763	The menu lists the thirteen styles, then **None**. It has no keyboard shortcuts. It works on every selected clip at once, as one undo step called **Set Transition**, and what each clip gets depends on where it sits.
764	
765	| Where the clip sits | What happens |
766	| --- | --- |
767	| It starts exactly where the clip before it ends | A new overlap is made. See [At a hard cut](#at-a-hard-cut). |
768	| It already overlaps the clip before it | It gets the new style. See [Restyle an overlap](#restyle-an-overlap). |
769	| After a gap, or first on its track | Nothing. See [Clips that are skipped](#clips-that-are-skipped). |
770	
771	A style is available only when at least one selected clip is at a hard cut or an overlap. **None** is available for any selection.
772	
773	The checkmark shows the style of the earliest selected clip, or **None** when that clip has no transition.
774	
775	## At a hard cut
776	
777	A clip that starts exactly where the clip before it ends gets a new half-second overlap, centred on the cut.
778	
779	The overlap is made from footage the two clips aren't showing. The first clip plays on past its out point, and the second starts earlier than its in point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the outer edges of the pair stay where they were.
780	
781	If there isn't half a second to spare, the transition comes out shorter. The length is limited by:
782	
783	- The footage each clip has beyond the cut. When one side runs short, the other side gives more if it can, so the overlap can end up off-centre.
784	- The neighbours. The first clip can't grow into the clip after the second, and the second can't grow into the clip before the first.
785	- [The overlap rules](/motion/transitions/), which hold an overlap to half the shorter clip.
786	
787	Text, shape, still, image and graphic clips have no file to run out of, so they can always give their share. A [nest](/editing/nests/) clip gives nothing before its start, and past its end it gives only what's left of the nest.
788	
789	The incoming clip now starts earlier, and what's timed to its picture stays in step. Its [actions](/motion/actions/) stay on the frames they were drawn over, so a zoom stays on its click, and timed caption words stay on their speech. A fade-in or a text reveal now starts at the clip's new first frame, so it begins under the transition.
790	
791	If the clip still holds a transition from an earlier overlap, it takes the style you chose and keeps that transition's curve and crossfade. Otherwise the new transition starts with the [default values](/motion/transition-settings/#default-values).
792	
793	## Restyle an overlap
794	
795	A clip that already overlaps the clip before it takes the style you choose, and keeps its curve and crossfade. The **Kind** row in [the Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/#kind) does the same for one clip.
796	
797	## Clips that are skipped
798	
799	A clip after a gap has nothing to overlap, and neither does the first clip on its track, so the menu skips them. If you select a run of clips that starts after a gap or at the start of its track, the first one is skipped and every cut after it gets the style.
800	
801	## No extra footage
802	
803	Two clips that each use their whole file have nothing beyond the cut to overlap with. When none of the cuts you chose can take a transition, Frame Job shows a sheet that says "There’s no extra footage at this cut for a transition.", or "at these cuts" for several.
804	
805	| Button | What it does |
806	| --- | --- |
807	| **Shift Clips Left** | Makes the overlap another way. See [Shift Clips Left](#shift-clips-left). |
808	| **Cancel** | Changes nothing. |
809	
810	A cut with footage to spare gets a shorter transition instead of the sheet, unless its clips are so short that the overlap rules leave no room for even one frame. If you chose several cuts and at least one takes a transition, there's no sheet either, and the cuts with no footage stay as they are.
811	
812	## Shift Clips Left
813	
814	**Shift Clips Left** makes the overlap by sliding the second clip, and everything after it on unlocked tracks, left by half a second. The second clip's first frames then blend over the first clip's last ones.
815	
816	- The project gets shorter by the same amount.
817	- No clip's footage changes.
818	- The shift is capped at half the shorter clip, and at the longest shift that keeps every moved track within [the overlap rules](/motion/transitions/).
819	- Markers don't move.
820	- A clip on another track that ends up overlapping its neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve.
821	- Clips on locked tracks stay where they are, so they fall out of step with what moved.
822	- The whole shift is one undo step, **Add Transition**, however many cuts it covers.
823	
824	Frame Job won't shift a second clip on a locked track. With only that cut chosen it beeps and nothing moves.
825	
826	## Overlap two clips by hand
827	
828	You can make a transition without the menu. When an edit makes a clip overlap the clip before it on the same track, and that clip has no stored transition, Frame Job adds a Cross Dissolve. That holds whether you drag, trim an edge, paste, add a clip, close a gap or shift clips.
829	
830	See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/) for the overlap rules, and [Default values](/motion/transition-settings/#default-values) for how that Cross Dissolve starts out.
831	
832	## Remove a transition
833	
834	Select the later clip of the pair and choose **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ None**, or choose **None** in the **Kind** row of [the Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/#kind).
835	
836	**None** in the menu is available for any selected clip, because a clip can hold a transition the timeline doesn't draw, such as one left behind when an overlap was dragged apart. It clears every selected clip, wherever each one sits.
837	
838	### None keeps the overlap
839	
840	**None** removes the transition but not the overlap. While the two clips still overlap they keep blending, as a plain linear dissolve with no hatch and no sound crossfade.
841	
842	To get a hard cut back, move or trim the clips so they no longer overlap.
843	
844	:::caution
845	An overlap with no transition doesn't stay that way. The next time you move or trim a clip on that track, or change the overlap's **Duration**, Frame Job gives it a Cross Dissolve again.
846	:::
847	
848	A transition you don't clear stays on the clip after you pull the overlap apart. It draws nothing until the clip overlaps something again, then comes back with its style. Choose **None** as well if you don't want that.
849	
850	## Good to know
851	
852	- An adjustment clip can't take a transition, on either side of a cut. Fade it with opacity instead. At a hard cut beside one, the no-extra-footage sheet still appears, and **Shift Clips Left** only beeps.
853	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the menu works on the clips inside it.
854	
855	## With an agent
856	
857	The menu uses the same two tools: `add_transition` for a clip at a hard cut, and `set_transition` for a clip that already overlaps.
858	
859	`add_transition` needs a `clip` and a `duration`. The menu always asks for half a second, centred on the cut. An agent can ask for any length of one frame or more, take the footage from [one side of the cut](/motion/transition-settings/#alignment), or shift clips with `ripple: true`, without going through the sheet. A request too long for the footage lands shorter, and a length that rounds to no frames at all is an error. With no `kind`, it uses the style the clip already holds, or Cross Dissolve if it holds none. The tool only works at a hard cut. On any other clip it fails, saying whether the clip is first on its track, follows a gap or already overlaps.
860	
861	`set_transition` needs a `clip` and a `kind`. Setting `kind: null` removes the transition, and because `kind` is required, leaving it out by mistake can't clear one. The tool can also put a style on a clip with no overlap, where it draws nothing until the clip overlaps something. See [`add_transition`](/mcp/tools-transitions/#add_transition) and [`set_transition`](/mcp/tools-transitions/#set_transition).
862

870	=================== transition-styles
871	---
872	title: "Transition styles"
873	description: "What each of the thirteen transition styles looks like, and how each one treats small layers and clips of different sizes."
874	---
875	
876	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
877	
878	A transition's style decides how one clip gives way to the next across their overlap. Frame Job has thirteen: Cross Dissolve, two fades, four pushes, four wipes, Slide and Zoom.
879	
880	<AtAGlance
881	  menu="Clip ▸ Transition ▸"
882	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition ▸ Kind"
883	  tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition']}
884	/>
885	
886	To put a style on a cut, see [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/). To change how it's eased or how long it lasts, see [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
887	
888	## Cross Dissolve
889	
890	The outgoing clip fades out as the incoming clip fades in. The two always add up to a whole picture, so the frame doesn't dip dark in the middle.
891	
892	Where only one of the two clips covers part of the canvas, that part fades to whatever is behind it.
893	
894	This is the style Frame Job uses when it adds a transition without being asked, such as when you drag one clip over the end of another.
895	
896	## Fade Through Black and Fade Through White
897	
898	**Fade Through Black** takes the outgoing clip down to black over the first half of the transition. At the halfway point the clips swap, and the incoming clip fades up from black over the second half.
899	
900	**Fade Through White** does the same through white. In an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the white is SDR white as it sits in that project, not the brightest white HLG can show.
901	
902	The two clips are never on screen together. See [Fades on small layers](#fades-on-small-layers) for what these styles do to a clip that doesn't fill the canvas.
903	
904	## Push
905	
906	Both clips move together, as if the incoming clip were shoving the outgoing one off the canvas.
907	
908	| Style | The outgoing clip leaves | The incoming clip comes in from |
909	| --- | --- | --- |
910	| **Push Left** | To the left | The right |
911	| **Push Right** | To the right | The left |
912	| **Push Up** | Upward | The bottom |
913	| **Push Down** | Downward | The top |
914	
915	## Wipe
916	
917	An edge sweeps across the picture, taking the outgoing clip away and revealing the incoming clip behind it. Neither clip moves. The edge is very slightly soft, so it doesn't crawl.
918	
919	| Style | The edge sweeps |
920	| --- | --- |
921	| **Wipe** | Left to right |
922	| **Wipe Left** | Right to left |
923	| **Wipe Up** | Bottom to top |
924	| **Wipe Down** | Top to bottom |
925	
926	## Slide
927	
928	The incoming clip slides in from the right over the outgoing clip, which stays where it is. Slide only comes in from the right. For the other directions, use a [Push](#push).
929	
930	## Zoom
931	
932	The outgoing clip grows toward you, from 100% to 125% of its size, while the incoming clip grows into place from 75% to 100%. The two dissolve into each other as they go. Each clip grows around its own centre.
933	
934	## Small layers and clips of different sizes
935	
936	A transition plays on each clip where that clip sits, not on the canvas as a whole. You won't see any of what follows on two full-frame clips of the same size. It matters for a picture-in-picture, or for a pair that differ in size, position, crop or rotation.
937	
938	### Wipes on mismatched clips
939	
940	A wipe's edge is measured in each clip's own frame, so two clips of different sizes don't meet at one line. Halfway through, the edge is halfway across each clip, wherever each one sits. The frame is the clip as it's cropped and placed, so on a rotated clip the edge turns with the clip.
941	
942	Between the two edges you can see whatever is behind the pair, or both clips at once.
943	
944	### Fades on small layers
945	
946	A fade through a colour changes the clip's own pixels toward that colour. On a clip smaller than the canvas, such as a picture-in-picture, you see a black or white box over what's behind it, not a see-through fade.
947	
948	For a small clip that should melt into the picture behind it, use [Cross Dissolve](#cross-dissolve).
949	
950	### Push and Slide on small layers
951	
952	A Push or a Slide always travels one whole canvas width, or one whole canvas height for Push Up and Push Down, whatever the size of the clip. A small incoming clip starts one canvas away from where it lands, so it doesn't begin at the edge of the frame unless it's placed there.
953	
954	Slide leaves the outgoing clip at full strength until the overlap ends. If the incoming clip is smaller, the outgoing clip stays visible around it for the whole transition, then disappears when the overlap ends.
955	
956	## Good to know
957	
958	- The style only changes the picture. Whether the sound crossfades is a separate choice, and it works the same with all thirteen. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/).
959	- A clip always draws with the Normal blend mode during a transition, whatever [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/) it has.
960	- Cross Dissolve and Zoom treat a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip as one picture. The other styles play on each layer inside the nest, so a wipe's edge is measured in each layer's own frame.
961	
962	## With an agent
963	
964	An agent names a style by its `kind`, which is the style's name in lower case with underscores: `cross_dissolve`, `push_left`, `wipe_up`, `slide`. The plain **Wipe** is `wipe`, and the two fades are `fade_black` and `fade_white`. See [Tools: transitions](/mcp/tools-transitions/).
965

974	title: "The Transition section"
975	description: "Set one transition's style, easing and length in the inspector, and see what values a new transition starts with."
976	---
977	
978	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
979	
980	The **Transition** section is where you fine-tune one transition: its style, how it's eased and how long it lasts.
981	
982	<AtAGlance
983	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition"
984	  tools={['set_transition', 'set_transition_style', 'set_transition_duration']}
985	/>
986	
987	## Open the section
988	
989	Select the later clip of an overlapping pair, then look on the **Clip** sub-tab of the [Clip tab](/getting-started/inspector/). A transition belongs to the clip it leads into, so the earlier clip of the pair won't show it unless it overlaps a clip before it too.
990	
991	The section appears only when exactly one clip is selected and that clip overlaps the clip before it. To change several transitions at once, use [**Clip ▸ Transition ▸**](/motion/add-a-transition/#the-transition-menu).
992	
993	It starts closed. Its header sums it up, for example "cross dissolve · ease in out · 0.50 s", or "none" when the overlap has no stored transition.
994	
995	| Row | What it does | Values |
996	| --- | --- | --- |
997	| [**Kind**](#kind) | The style, or none | None and the thirteen [styles](/motion/transition-styles/) |
998	| [**Curve**](#curve) | How the transition's progress is eased | Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out |
999	| **Crossfade Audio** | Whether the sound crossfades. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/). | On or off |
1000	| **Crossfade Shape** | The crossfade's curve. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/). | Linear, S-Curve, +3 dB, −3 dB |
1001	| [**Duration**](#duration) | The length of the overlap | 0.02 to 10 s |
1002	
1003	Each change is one undo step.
1004	
1005	## Kind
1006	
1007	**Kind** lists **None**, then the thirteen styles in the same order as the **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** menu. Changing the style keeps the **Curve** and the crossfade settings.
1008	
1009	Choosing **None** removes the transition but not the overlap. See [None keeps the overlap](/motion/add-a-transition/#none-keeps-the-overlap).
1010	
1011	## Curve
1012	
1013	**Curve** changes how the transition moves through its length, not how long it lasts.
1014	
1015	| Curve | How it moves |
1016	| --- | --- |
1017	| **Linear** | At a steady rate from start to finish |
1018	| **Ease In** | Starts slowly and speeds up |
1019	| **Ease Out** | Starts quickly and slows down |
1020	| **Ease In Out** | Starts and ends slowly |
1021	
1022	The sound crossfade follows the same curve.
1023	
1024	The curve also moves the swap in a [Fade Through Black or White](/motion/transition-styles/#fade-through-black-and-fade-through-white). With **Linear** or **Ease In Out** the clips swap halfway through the overlap. With **Ease In** it's about 71% of the way through, and with **Ease Out** about 29%.
1025	
1026	## Duration
1027	
1028	**Duration** is the length of the overlap, in seconds. Type a value, or pick 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 from the arrow at the end of the field. A number outside 0.02 to 10 s is pulled to the nearer end of that range, and the result snaps to the frame grid. A value that rounds to no frames at all closes the overlap and leaves a hard cut.
1029	
1030	The overlap is the transition's length, so changing **Duration** moves the later clip to match: earlier for a longer transition, later for a shorter one. Only that clip moves.
1031	
1032	- Clips after it stay where they are, so a longer transition can open a gap after the clip.
1033	- A shorter transition can run the clip into the one after it, and that new overlap gets a Cross Dissolve.
1034	- A linked clip doesn't move with it.
1035	
1036	Frame Job won't let an overlap pass half the shorter clip, or move the clip anywhere that breaks [the overlap rules](/motion/transitions/) with its other neighbours. The message at the foot of the inspector names the limit, and nothing changes.
1037	
1038	## Alignment
1039	
1040	Alignment decides which clip's footage a new overlap at a hard cut is made from. The section has no control for it. **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** always centres a new overlap on the cut: half of it comes from each clip, an odd frame comes from the incoming clip, and a side that runs short passes its share to the other.
1041	
1042	An agent can choose the side with the `align` argument of `add_transition`:
1043	
1044	| Choice | Where the footage comes from | What stays put |
1045	| --- | --- | --- |
1046	| `center`, the default | Half from each clip | The moment of the cut |
1047	| `before` | All from the start of the incoming clip | The outgoing clip's last frame |
1048	| `after` | All from the end of the outgoing clip | The incoming clip's first frame |
1049	
1050	## Default values
1051	
1052	A transition Frame Job makes starts with **Curve** at **Ease In Out** and **Crossfade Audio** on, with **Crossfade Shape** at **+3 dB**. When you didn't choose a style, it's a Cross Dissolve.
1053	
1054	[An overlap with no stored transition](/motion/transitions/#an-overlap-with-no-stored-transition), such as one you set to **None**, draws as a linear Cross Dissolve with no crossfade. The section says so: **Kind** reads **None**, **Curve** reads **Linear** and **Crossfade Audio** is off. From there:
1055	
1056	- Changing **Curve** or **Crossfade Audio** stores a Cross Dissolve with exactly the values showing, and your one change. **Crossfade Shape** stays dimmed until **Crossfade Audio** is on.
1057	- Choosing a **Kind** makes a new transition with the defaults above, not the values that were showing.
1058	
1059	## Good to know
1060	
1061	Two overlapping clips with no picture get the same section. Only their sound changes, so **Kind** has no visible effect.
1062	
1063	## With an agent
1064	
1065	`set_transition_style` sets **Curve**, **Crossfade Audio** and **Crossfade Shape** through `curve`, `audio` and `audio_shape`. Anything left out stays as it is, and leaving out all three is an error. Unlike the section, it works on any clip but an adjustment clip. A clip with no transition gets a Cross Dissolve with that style.
1066	
1067	`set_transition_duration` does what **Duration** does, and it fails on the first clip of a track, which has nothing to overlap. A length that rounds to no frames is an error there, where **Duration** closes the overlap. `set_transition` sets **Kind**.
1068	
1069	See [`set_transition_style`](/mcp/tools-transitions/#set_transition_style), [`set_transition_duration`](/mcp/tools-transitions/#set_transition_duration) and [`set_transition`](/mcp/tools-transitions/#set_transition).
1070

28	An action makes a clip change over time: a zoom into a screen recording, a fade of the volume, a title that slides and changes colour. You say where the clip ends up, and the action's span and curve say how it gets there.
29	
30	<AtAGlance
31	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
32	  keys="⌥⌘K"
33	  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', "A band on the clip in the timeline"]}
34	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
35	/>
36	
37	<Shot
38	  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.window"
39	  alt="The editor with a lower third selected. On the timeline the graphic clip holds a numbered action band, the Clip tab's action lane reads 1, editing 1, and the inspector shows the values the clip reaches at the action's end."
